2512.23437.title: RealX3D: A Physically-Degraded 3D Benchmark for Multi-view Visual Restoration and Reconstruction

screening.reason: The paper introduces a benchmark dataset specifically for evaluating multi-view 3D reconstruction under physical degradations, which is directly useful for testing core geometry models.
screening.evidence: We introduce RealX3D, a real-capture benchmark for multi-view visual restoration and 3D reconstruction under diverse physical degradations.
screening.task: multi-view visual restoration and 3D reconstruction

2512.23437.abstract: We introduce RealX3D, a real-capture benchmark for multi-view visual restoration and 3D reconstruction under diverse physical degradations. RealX3D groups corruptions into four families, including illumination, scattering, occlusion, and blurring, and captures each at multiple severity levels using a unified acquisition protocol that yields pixel-aligned LQ/GT views. Each scene includes high-resolution capture, RAW images, and dense laser scans, from which we derive world-scale meshes and metric depth. Benchmarking a broad range of optimization-based and feed-forward methods shows substantial degradation in reconstruction quality under physical corruptions, underscoring the fragility of current multi-view pipelines in real-world challenging environments.

2512.10267.title: Long-LRM++: Preserving Fine Details in Feed-Forward Wide-Coverage Reconstruction

screening.reason: Long-LRM++ is a feed-forward method that reconstructs 3D scenes from unposed images (32-64 views), placing it in the same core family as DUSt3R. Its main contribution is a semi-explicit representation with a lightweight decoder for better rendering quality and real-time speed, which is a narrower improvement rather than a new geometry prediction paradigm, making 4 more appropriate than 5.
screening.evidence: feed-forward reconstruction of scenes from tens of input views
screening.task: feed-forward 3D scene reconstruction from unposed images with real-time rendering

2512.10267.abstract: Recent advances in generalizable Gaussian splatting (GS) have enabled feed-forward reconstruction of scenes from tens of input views. Long-LRM notably scales this paradigm to 32 input images at $950\times540$ resolution, achieving 360° scene-level reconstruction in a single forward pass. However, directly predicting millions of Gaussian parameters at once remains highly error-sensitive: small inaccuracies in positions or other attributes lead to noticeable blurring, particularly in fine structures such as text. In parallel, implicit representation methods such as LVSM and LaCT have demonstrated significantly higher rendering fidelity by compressing scene information into model weights rather than explicit Gaussians, and decoding RGB frames using the full transformer or TTT backbone. However, this computationally intensive decompression process for every rendered frame makes real-time rendering infeasible. These observations raise key questions: Is the deep, sequential "decompression" process necessary? Can we retain the benefits of implicit representations while enabling real-time performance? We address these questions with Long-LRM++, a model that adopts a semi-explicit scene representation combined with a lightweight decoder. Long-LRM++ matches the rendering quality of LaCT on DL3DV while achieving real-time 14 FPS rendering on an A100 GPU, overcoming the speed limitations of prior implicit methods. Our design also scales to 64 input views at the $950\times540$ resolution, demonstrating strong generalization to increased input lengths. Additionally, Long-LRM++ delivers superior novel-view depth prediction on ScanNetv2 compared to direct depth rendering from Gaussians. Extensive ablation studies validate the effectiveness of each component in the proposed framework.
2512.10267.authors: Chen Ziwen, Hao Tan, Peng Wang, Zexiang Xu, Li Fuxin

2512.07165.title: MuSASplat: Efficient Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splats via Lightweight Multi-Scale Adaptation

screening.reason: MuSASplat directly predicts 3D Gaussian splats from unposed images, which qualifies as core per the criteria for reconstructable scene representations from unposed inputs. screening.evidence: pose-free feed-forward 3D Gaussian splats models
screening.task: sparse-view novel view synthesis via 3D Gaussian splatting from unposed images

2512.07165.abstract: Sparse-view 3D Gaussian splatting seeks to render high-quality novel views of 3D scenes from a limited set of input images. While recent pose-free feed-forward methods leveraging pre-trained 3D priors have achieved impressive results, most of them rely on full fine-tuning of large Vision Transformer (ViT) backbones and incur substantial GPU costs. In this work, we introduce MuSASplat, a novel framework that dramatically reduces the computational burden of training pose-free feed-forward 3D Gaussian splats models with little compromise of rendering quality. Central to our approach is a lightweight Multi-Scale Adapter that enables efficient fine-tuning of ViT-based architectures with only a small fraction of training parameters. This design avoids the prohibitive GPU overhead associated with previous full-model adaptation techniques while maintaining high fidelity in novel view synthesis, even with very sparse input views. In addition, we introduce a Feature Fusion Aggregator that integrates features across input views effectively and efficiently. Unlike widely adopted memory banks, the Feature Fusion Aggregator ensures consistent geometric integration across input views and meanwhile mitigates the memory usage, training complexity, and computational costs significantly. Extensive experiments across diverse datasets show that MuSASplat achieves state-of-the-art rendering quality but has significantly reduced parameters and training resource requirements as compared with existing methods.

screening.evidence: feed-forward methods have emerged as efficient and robust alternatives to traditional per-scene optimization techniques
screening.task: efficient feed-forward 3D reconstruction from multi-view unposed images

2512.01540.abstract: 3D reconstruction from multi-view images is a core challenge in computer vision. Recently, feed-forward methods have emerged as efficient and robust alternatives to traditional per-scene optimization techniques. Among them, state-of-the-art models like the Visual Geometry Grounding Transformer (VGGT) leverage full self-attention over all image tokens to capture global relationships. However, this approach suffers from poor scalability due to the quadratic complexity of self-attention and the large number of tokens generated in long image sequences. In this work, we introduce FlashVGGT, an efficient alternative that addresses this bottleneck through a descriptor-based attention mechanism. Instead of applying dense global attention across all tokens, FlashVGGT compresses spatial information from each frame into a compact set of descriptor tokens. Global attention is then computed as cross-attention between the full set of image tokens and this smaller descriptor set, significantly reducing computational overhead. Moreover, the compactness of the descriptors enables online inference over long sequences via a chunk-recursive mechanism that reuses cached descriptors from previous chunks. Experimental results show that FlashVGGT achieves reconstruction accuracy competitive with VGGT while reducing inference time to just 9.3% of VGGT for 1,000 images, and scaling efficiently to sequences exceeding 3,000 images. Our project page is available at https://wzpscott.github.io/flashvggt_page/.

2512.00771.title: EAG3R: Event-Augmented 3D Geometry Estimation for Dynamic and Extreme-Lighting Scenes

screening.reason: EAG3R is built on the MonST3R backbone and augments pointmap-based reconstruction with event streams and new modules, making it a substantive extension of the DUSt3R model family. The narrower scope (event-augmented, extreme-lighting scenarios) distinguishes it from a 5.

screening.task: pose-free 3D geometry estimation from image pairs augmented with event streams

2512.00771.abstract: Robust 3D geometry estimation from videos is critical for applications such as autonomous navigation, SLAM, and 3D scene reconstruction. Recent methods like DUSt3R demonstrate that regressing dense pointmaps from image pairs enables accurate and efficient pose-free reconstruction. However, existing RGB-only approaches struggle under real-world conditions involving dynamic objects and extreme illumination, due to the inherent limitations of conventional cameras. In this paper, we propose EAG3R, a novel geometry estimation framework that augments pointmap-based reconstruction with asynchronous event streams. Built upon the MonST3R backbone, EAG3R introduces two key innovations: (1) a retinex-inspired image enhancement module and a lightweight event adapter with SNR-aware fusion mechanism that adaptively combines RGB and event features based on local reliability; and (2) a novel event-based photometric consistency loss that reinforces spatiotemporal coherence during global optimization. Our method enables robust geometry estimation in challenging dynamic low-light scenes without requiring retraining on night-time data. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EAG3R significantly outperforms state-of-the-art RGB-only baselines across monocular depth estimation, camera pose tracking, and dynamic reconstruction tasks.

2511.22429.title: Fin3R: Fine-tuning Feed-forward 3D Reconstruction Models via Monocular Knowledge Distillation

screening.reason: Fin3R is a fine-tuning method that directly improves the DUSt3R family of pointmap-regression models by distilling monocular geometry into their encoders, validated on DUSt3R, MASt3R, CUT3R, and VGGT. It is a training technique rather than a new architecture, placing it at 4 rather than 5.
screening.evidence: We validate our method on a wide range of models, including DUSt3R, MASt3R, CUT3R, and VGGT
screening.task: fine-tuning feed-forward 3D reconstruction models via monocular knowledge distillation

2511.22429.abstract: We present Fin3R, a simple, effective, and general fine-tuning method for feed-forward 3D reconstruction models. The family of feed-forward reconstruction model regresses pointmap of all input images to a reference frame coordinate system, along with other auxiliary outputs, in a single forward pass. However, we find that current models struggle with fine geometry and robustness due to (\textit{i}) the scarcity of high-fidelity depth and pose supervision and (\textit{ii}) the inherent geometric misalignment from multi-view pointmap regression. Fin3R jointly tackles two issues with an extra lightweight fine-tuning step. We freeze the decoder, which handles view matching, and fine-tune only the image encoder-the component dedicated to feature extraction. The encoder is enriched with fine geometric details distilled from a strong monocular teacher model on large, unlabeled datasets, using a custom, lightweight LoRA adapter. We validate our method on a wide range of models, including DUSt3R, MASt3R, CUT3R, and VGGT. The fine-tuned models consistently deliver sharper boundaries, recover complex structures, and achieve higher geometric accuracy in both single- and multi-view settings, while adding only the tiny LoRA weights, which leave test-time memory and latency virtually unchanged. Project page: \href{http://visual-ai.github.io/fin3r}{https://visual-ai.github.io/fin3r}
2511.22429.authors: Weining Ren, Hongjun Wang, Xiao Tan, Kai Han

2511.18386.title: SegSplat: Feed-forward Gaussian Splatting and Open-Set Semantic Segmentation

screening.reason: SegSplat directly predicts 3D Gaussians (geometry and appearance) from multi-view images in a single feed-forward pass, qualifying as a comparable model that reconstructs dense scene geometry from unposed images. However, the primary novelty is the open-set semantic segmentation layer, and the geometry is described as comparable to existing feed-forward methods rather than being the central contribution, making score 5 less appropriate.
screening.evidence: predicting discrete semantic indices alongside geometric and appearance attributes for each 3D Gaussian in a single pass
screening.task: feed-forward 3D Gaussian reconstruction with open-set semantic segmentation
outputs: 3D Gaussians with geometric and appearance attributes

2511.18386.abstract: We have introduced SegSplat, a novel framework designed to bridge the gap between rapid, feed-forward 3D reconstruction and rich, open-vocabulary semantic understanding. By constructing a compact semantic memory bank from multi-view 2D foundation model features and predicting discrete semantic indices alongside geometric and appearance attributes for each 3D Gaussian in a single pass, SegSplat efficiently imbues scenes with queryable semantics. Our experiments demonstrate that SegSplat achieves geometric fidelity comparable to state-of-the-art feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting methods while simultaneously enabling robust open-set semantic segmentation, crucially \textit{without} requiring any per-scene optimization for semantic feature integration. This work represents a significant step towards practical, on-the-fly generation of semantically aware 3D environments, vital for advancing robotic interaction, augmented reality, and other intelligent systems.
2511.18386.authors: Peter Siegel, Federico Tombari, Marc Pollefeys, Daniel Barath

2511.12040.title: SRSplat: Feed-Forward Super-Resolution Gaussian Splatting from Sparse Multi-View Images

screening.reason: SRSplat directly predicts 3D Gaussians from unposed multi-view images, which is the core task, but its scope is narrower as it specializes in super-resolution from low-resolution inputs and depends on externally generated reference images from MLLMs and diffusion models.
screening.evidence: a feed-forward framework that reconstructs high-resolution 3D scenes from only a few LR views
screening.task: feed-forward 3D Gaussian reconstruction from sparse low-resolution multi-view images

2511.12040.abstract: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction from sparse, low-resolution (LR) images is a crucial capability for real-world applications, such as autonomous driving and embodied AI. However, existing methods often fail to recover fine texture details. This limitation stems from the inherent lack of high-frequency information in LR inputs. To address this, we propose \textbf{SRSplat}, a feed-forward framework that reconstructs high-resolution 3D scenes from only a few LR views. Our main insight is to compensate for the deficiency of texture information by jointly leveraging external high-quality reference images and internal texture cues. We first construct a scene-specific reference gallery, generated for each scene using Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) and diffusion models. To integrate this external information, we introduce the \textit{Reference-Guided Feature Enhancement (RGFE)} module, which aligns and fuses features from the LR input images and their reference twin image. Subsequently, we train a decoder to predict the Gaussian primitives using the multi-view fused feature obtained from \textit{RGFE}. To further refine predicted Gaussian primitives, we introduce \textit{Texture-Aware Density Control (TADC)}, which adaptively adjusts Gaussian density based on the internal texture richness of the LR inputs. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our SRSplat outperforms existing methods on various datasets, including RealEstate10K, ACID, and DTU, and exhibits strong cross-dataset and cross-resolution generalization capabilities.
2511.12040.authors: Xinyuan Hu, Changyue Shi, Chuxiao Yang, Minghao Chen, Jiajun Ding, Tao Wei, Chen Wei, Zhou Yu, Min Tan

2511.09818.title: Lumos3D: A Single-Forward Framework for Low-Light 3D Scene Restoration

screening.reason: Lumos3D is a pose-free, feed-forward framework that directly reconstructs 3D Gaussian scenes from unposed multi-view images, fitting the core criterion of predicting a reconstructable scene representation from unposed inputs. Its scope is narrower than DUSt3R/MASt3R because it targets the low-light domain specifically and uses a distillation scheme rather than a novel architecture, placing it at 4 rather than 5.
screening.evidence: directly restoring illumination and structure from unposed, low-light multi-view images without any per-scene training or optimization
screening.task: low-light 3D scene restoration from unposed multi-view images

2511.09818.abstract: Restoring 3D scenes with low-light conditions is challenging, and most existing methods depend on precomputed camera poses and scene-specific optimization, which greatly restricts their application to real-world scenarios. To overcome these limitations, we propose Lumos3D, a pose-free single-forward framework for 3D low-light scene restoration. First, we develop a cross-illumination distillation scheme, where a frozen teacher network takes normal-light ground truth images as input to distill accurate geometric information to the student model. Second, we define a Lumos loss to improve the restoration quality of the reconstructed 3D Gaussian space. Trained on a single dataset, Lumos3D performs inference in a purely feed-forward manner, directly restoring illumination and structure from unposed, low-light multi-view images without any per-scene training or optimization. Experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that Lumos3D achieves competitive restoration results compared to scene-specific methods. Our codes are available at https://github.com/HanzhouLiu/Lumos3D.
2511.09818.authors: Hanzhou Liu, Peng Jiang, Jia Huang, Mi Lu

2511.03970.title: Room Envelopes: A Synthetic Dataset for Indoor Layout Reconstruction from Images

screening.reason: The paper introduces a synthetic dataset providing pointmap supervision for feed-forward geometry estimators, which is the same output representation as DUSt3R, but the task is narrower (indoor structural layout) rather than general dense scene reconstruction from unposed images. A score of 5 is less appropriate because the dataset's stated purpose targets indoor layout reconstruction specifically, not the general core problem.
screening.evidence: direct supervision for feed-forward monocular geometry estimators that predict both the first visible surface and the first layout surface
screening.task: indoor layout reconstruction from images

2511.03970.abstract: Modern scene reconstruction methods are able to accurately recover 3D surfaces that are visible in one or more images. However, this leads to incomplete reconstructions, missing all occluded surfaces. While much progress has been made on reconstructing entire objects given partial observations using generative models, the structural elements of a scene, like the walls, floors and ceilings, have received less attention. We argue that these scene elements should be relatively easy to predict, since they are typically planar, repetitive and simple, and so less costly approaches may be suitable. In this work, we present a synthetic dataset -- Room Envelopes -- that facilitates progress on this task by providing a set of RGB images and two associated pointmaps for each image: one capturing the visible surface and one capturing the first surface once fittings and fixtures are removed, that is, the structural layout. As we show, this enables direct supervision for feed-forward monocular geometry estimators that predict both the first visible surface and the first layout surface. This confers an understanding of the scene's extent, as well as the shape and location of its objects.

2510.10097.title: Gesplat: Robust Pose-Free 3D Reconstruction via Geometry-Guided Gaussian Splatting

screening.reason: Gesplat directly reconstructs 3D Gaussian scenes from unposed sparse images, placing it in the same category as NoPoSplat and AnySplat, but its reliance on VGGT as an external foundation model for initialization makes it slightly less self-contained than a fully end-to-end core model like DUSt3R or MASt3R.
screening.evidence: robust novel view synthesis and geometrically consistent reconstruction from unposed sparse images
screening.task: pose-free 3D reconstruction and novel view synthesis from sparse images

2510.10097.abstract: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) have advanced 3D reconstruction and novel view synthesis, but remain heavily dependent on accurate camera poses and dense viewpoint coverage. These requirements limit their applicability in sparse-view settings, where pose estimation becomes unreliable and supervision is insufficient. To overcome these challenges, we introduce Gesplat, a 3DGS-based framework that enables robust novel view synthesis and geometrically consistent reconstruction from unposed sparse images. Unlike prior works that rely on COLMAP for sparse point cloud initialization, we leverage the VGGT foundation model to obtain more reliable initial poses and dense point clouds. Our approach integrates several key innovations: 1) a hybrid Gaussian representation with dual position-shape optimization enhanced by inter-view matching consistency; 2) a graph-guided attribute refinement module to enhance scene details; and 3) flow-based depth regularization that improves depth estimation accuracy for more effective supervision. Comprehensive quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves more robust performance on both forward-facing and large-scale complex datasets compared to other pose-free methods.

2510.07856.title: XYZCylinder: Towards Compatible Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting for Driving Scenes via Unified Cylinder Lifting Method

screening.reason: The paper introduces a feed-forward method that directly predicts 3D Gaussians (a reconstructable scene representation) from images with varying camera configurations, fitting the core criteria of reconstructing dense geometry from unposed images. The narrower scope is that it is specifically designed for driving scenes with a cylinder-based lifting approach, making it less general than DUSt3R or MASt3R.
screening.evidence: a novel method built upon a unified cylinder lifting method that integrates camera modeling and feature lifting
screening.task: feed-forward 3D scene reconstruction from images with varying camera configurations

2510.07856.abstract: Feed-forward paradigms for 3D reconstruction have become a focus of recent research, which learn implicit, fixed view transformations to generate a single scene representation. However, their application to complex driving scenes reveals significant limitations. Two core challenges are responsible for this performance gap. First, the reliance on a fixed view transformation hinders compatibility to varying camera configurations. Second, the inherent difficulty of learning complex driving scenes from sparse 360° views with minimal overlap compromises the final reconstruction fidelity. To handle these difficulties, we introduce XYZCylinder, a novel method built upon a unified cylinder lifting method that integrates camera modeling and feature lifting. To tackle the compatibility problem, we design a Unified Cylinder Camera Modeling (UCCM) strategy. This strategy explicitly models projection parameters to unify diverse camera setups, thus bypassing the need for learning viewpoint-dependent correspondences. To improve the reconstruction accuracy, we propose a hybrid representation with several dedicated modules based on newly designed Cylinder Plane Feature Group (CPFG) to lift 2D image features to 3D space. Extensive evaluations confirm that XYZCylinder not only achieves state-of-the-art performance under different evaluation settings but also demonstrates remarkable compatibility in entirely new scenes with different camera settings in a zero-shot manner. Project page: \href{https://yuyuyu223.github.io/XYZCYlinder-projectpage/}{here}

2509.26645.title: TTT3R: 3D Reconstruction as Test-Time Training

screening.reason: TTT3R is a training-free intervention that improves length generalization of existing 3R reconstruction models (CUT3R family) by deriving a closed-form learning rate for memory updates, making it a substantive extension of the model's streaming behavior rather than a new architecture. It scores 4 rather than 5 because it modifies inference behavior of existing models rather than introducing a new model or new prediction capability like MASt3R's feature head.
screening.evidence: This training-free intervention, termed TTT3R, substantially improves length generalization
screening.task: 3D reconstruction from streaming images with improved length generalization

2509.26645.abstract: Modern Recurrent Neural Networks have become a competitive architecture for 3D reconstruction due to their linear-time complexity. However, their performance degrades significantly when applied beyond the training context length, revealing limited length generalization. In this work, we revisit the 3D reconstruction foundation models from a Test-Time Training perspective, framing their designs as an online learning problem. Building on this perspective, we leverage the alignment confidence between the memory state and incoming observations to derive a closed-form learning rate for memory updates, to balance between retaining historical information and adapting to new observations. This training-free intervention, termed TTT3R, substantially improves length generalization, achieving a $2\times$ improvement in global pose estimation over baselines, while operating at 20 FPS with just 6 GB of GPU memory to process thousands of images. Code is available in https://rover-xingyu.github.io/TTT3R
2509.26645.authors: Xingyu Chen, Yue Chen, Yuliang Xiu, Andreas Geiger, Anpei Chen

2509.24209.title: Forge4D: Feed-Forward 4D Human Reconstruction and Interpolation from Uncalibrated Sparse-view Videos

screening.reason: Forge4D directly predicts 3D Gaussians from uncalibrated sparse-view images in a feed-forward manner, which qualifies as a core contribution of predicting a reconstructable scene representation from unposed images. screening.task: 4D human reconstruction and interpolation from uncalibrated sparse-view videos

2509.24209.abstract: Instant reconstruction of dynamic 3D humans from uncalibrated sparse-view videos is critical for numerous downstream applications. Existing methods, however, are either limited by the slow reconstruction speeds or incapable of generating novel-time representations. To address these challenges, we propose Forge4D, a feed-forward 4D human reconstruction and interpolation model that efficiently reconstructs temporally aligned representations from uncalibrated sparse-view videos, enabling both novel view and novel time synthesis. Our model simplifies the 4D reconstruction and interpolation problem as a joint task of streaming 3D Gaussian reconstruction and dense motion prediction. For the task of streaming 3D Gaussian reconstruction, we first reconstruct static 3D Gaussians from uncalibrated sparse-view images and then introduce learnable state tokens to enforce temporal consistency in a memory-friendly manner by interactively updating shared information across different timestamps. For novel time synthesis, we design a novel motion prediction module to predict dense motions for each 3D Gaussian between two adjacent frames, coupled with an occlusion-aware Gaussian fusion process to interpolate 3D Gaussians at arbitrary timestamps. To overcome the lack of the ground truth for dense motion supervision, we formulate dense motion prediction as a dense point matching task and introduce a self-supervised retargeting loss to optimize this module. An additional occlusion-aware optical flow loss is introduced to ensure motion consistency with plausible human movement, providing stronger regularization. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our model on both in-domain and out-of-domain datasets. Project page and code at: https://zhenliuzju.github.io/huyingdong/Forge4D.
2509.24209.authors: Yingdong Hu, Yisheng He, Jinnan Chen, Weihao Yuan, Kejie Qiu, Zehong Lin, Siyu Zhu, Zilong Dong, Steven Hoi, Jun Zhang

2509.23737.abstract: DUSt3R-based end-to-end scene reconstruction has recently shown promising results in dense visual SLAM. However, most existing methods only use image pairs to estimate pointmaps, overlooking spatial memory and global consistency.To this end, we introduce GRS-SLAM3R, an end-to-end SLAM framework for dense scene reconstruction and pose estimation from RGB images without any prior knowledge of the scene or camera parameters. Unlike existing DUSt3R-based frameworks, which operate on all image pairs and predict per-pair point maps in local coordinate frames, our method supports sequentialized input and incrementally estimates metric-scale point clouds in the global coordinate. In order to improve consistent spatial correlation, we use a latent state for spatial memory and design a transformer-based gated update module to reset and update the spatial memory that continuously aggregates and tracks relevant 3D information across frames. Furthermore, we partition the scene into submaps, apply local alignment within each submap, and register all submaps into a common world frame using relative constraints, producing a globally consistent map. Experiments on various datasets show that our framework achieves superior reconstruction accuracy while maintaining real-time performance.
2509.23737.authors: Guole Shen, Tianchen Deng, Yanbo Wang, Yongtao Chen, Yilin Shen, Jiuming Liu, Jingchuan Wang

2508.17972.title: SAIL-Recon: Large SfM by Augmenting Scene Regression with Localization

screening.reason: SAIL-Recon is a feed-forward Transformer that directly regresses camera poses and 3D scene structures from unposed images, making it a comparable model to DUSt3R. However, its main novelty is scaling to large scenes via fine-tuning conditioned on a neural scene representation (test-time training), and it is based on VGGT rather than extending DUSt3R's pointmap architecture, placing it at 4 rather than 5.
screening.evidence: a feed-forward Transformer for large scale SfM, by augmenting the scene regression network with visual localization capabilities
screening.task: large-scale Structure-from-Motion via scene regression

2508.17972.abstract: Scene regression methods, such as VGGT, solve the Structure-from-Motion (SfM) problem by directly regressing camera poses and 3D scene structures from input images. They demonstrate impressive performance in handling images under extreme viewpoint changes. However, these methods struggle to handle a large number of input images. To address this problem, we introduce SAIL-Recon, a feed-forward Transformer for large scale SfM, by augmenting the scene regression network with visual localization capabilities. Specifically, our method first computes a neural scene representation from a subset of anchor images. The regression network is then fine-tuned to reconstruct all input images conditioned on this neural scene representation. Comprehensive experiments show that our method not only scales efficiently to large-scale scenes, but also achieves state-of-the-art results on both camera pose estimation and novel view synthesis benchmarks, including TUM-RGBD, CO3Dv2, and Tanks & Temples. We will publish our model and code. Code and models are publicly available at: https://hkust-sail.github.io/ sail-recon/.

2507.22342.title: UFV-Splatter: Pose-Free Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting Adapted to Unfavorable Views

screening.reason: The paper presents a pose-free feed-forward 3DGS framework that directly predicts 3D Gaussians from unposed images, qualifying as core, but its contribution is an adaptation of pretrained models via LoRA and adapter modules rather than a new architecture, giving it narrower scope than a from-scratch model like NoPoSplat.
screening.evidence: pose-free, feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) framework designed to handle unfavorable input views
screening.task: pose-free 3D Gaussian Splatting from unfavorable views

2507.22342.abstract: This paper presents a pose-free, feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) framework designed to handle unfavorable input views. A common rendering setup for training feed-forward approaches places a 3D object at the world origin and renders it from cameras pointed toward the origin -- i.e., from favorable views, limiting the applicability of these models to real-world scenarios involving varying and unknown camera poses. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a novel adaptation framework that enables pretrained pose-free feed-forward 3DGS models to handle unfavorable views. We leverage priors learned from favorable images by feeding recentered images into a pretrained model augmented with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) layers. We further propose a Gaussian adapter module to enhance the geometric consistency of the Gaussians derived from the recentered inputs, along with a Gaussian alignment method to render accurate target views for training. Additionally, we introduce a new training strategy that utilizes an off-the-shelf dataset composed solely of favorable images. Experimental results on both synthetic images from the Google Scanned Objects dataset and real images from the OmniObject3D dataset validate the effectiveness of our method in handling unfavorable input views.
2507.22342.authors: Yuki Fujimura, Takahiro Kushida, Kazuya Kitano, Takuya Funatomi, Yasuhiro Mukaigawa

2506.09565.title: SemanticSplat: Feed-Forward 3D Scene Understanding with Language-Aware Gaussian Fields

screening.reason: SemanticSplat is a feed-forward method that directly predicts 3D Gaussians (a reconstructable scene representation) from sparse-view images, placing it in the same family as NoPoSplat/AnySplat. However, its primary novelty is the semantic-aware integration rather than the geometry prediction itself, making it a directly relevant core contribution with narrower scope (4) rather than a central model contribution (5).
screening.evidence: a feed-forward semantic-aware 3D reconstruction method, which unifies 3D Gaussians with latent semantic attributes for joint geometry-appearance-semantics modeling
screening.task: feed-forward 3D scene reconstruction with semantic attributes from sparse-view images

2506.09565.abstract: Holistic 3D scene understanding, which jointly models geometry, appearance, and semantics, is crucial for applications like augmented reality and robotic interaction. Existing feed-forward 3D scene understanding methods (e.g., LSM) are limited to extracting language-based semantics from scenes, failing to achieve holistic scene comprehension. Additionally, they suffer from low-quality geometry reconstruction and noisy artifacts. In contrast, per-scene optimization methods rely on dense input views, which reduces practicality and increases complexity during deployment. In this paper, we propose SemanticSplat, a feed-forward semantic-aware 3D reconstruction method, which unifies 3D Gaussians with latent semantic attributes for joint geometry-appearance-semantics modeling. To predict the semantic anisotropic Gaussians, SemanticSplat fuses diverse feature fields (e.g., LSeg, SAM) with a cost volume representation that stores cross-view feature similarities, enhancing coherent and accurate scene comprehension. Leveraging a two-stage distillation framework, SemanticSplat reconstructs a holistic multi-modal semantic feature field from sparse-view images. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method for 3D scene understanding tasks like promptable and open-vocabulary segmentation. Video results are available at https://semanticsplat.github.io.
2506.09565.authors: Qijing Li, Jingxiang Sun, Liang An, Zhaoqi Su, Hongwen Zhang, Yebin Liu

screening.reason: The paper introduces a benchmark dataset for 3D reconstruction from unposed cameras, directly targeting the core DUSt3R task, but its scope is narrower—specifically focused on altitude variation and large-scale scenes—making it a useful but domain-specific resource rather than a general benchmark for the core problem.

2505.00734.abstract: Production of photorealistic, navigable 3D site models requires a large volume of carefully collected images that are often unavailable to first responders for disaster relief or law enforcement. Real-world challenges include limited numbers of images, heterogeneous unposed cameras, inconsistent lighting, and extreme viewpoint differences for images collected from varying altitudes. To promote research aimed at addressing these challenges, we have developed the first public benchmark dataset for 3D reconstruction and novel view synthesis based on multiple calibrated ground-level, security-level, and airborne cameras. We present datasets that pose real-world challenges, independently evaluate calibration of unposed cameras and quality of novel rendered views, demonstrate baseline performance using recent state-of-practice methods, and identify challenges for further research.

2504.13419.title: Mono3R: Exploiting Monocular Cues for Geometric 3D Reconstruction

screening.reason: The paper proposes a monocular-guided refinement module that integrates monocular geometric priors into DUSt3R-style multi-view reconstruction, producing feed-forward point clouds and camera poses from unposed images. This is a substantive extension of the DUSt3R framework (analogous to MASt3R's feature head) but narrower in scope as a refinement module rather than a full architectural redesign, placing it at 4 rather than 5.
screening.evidence: we introduce a monocular-guided refinement module that integrates monocular geometric priors into multi-view reconstruction frameworks
screening.task: multi-view 3D reconstruction (point cloud and camera pose estimation) from unposed images

2504.13419.abstract: Recent advances in data-driven geometric multi-view 3D reconstruction foundation models (e.g., DUSt3R) have shown remarkable performance across various 3D vision tasks, facilitated by the release of large-scale, high-quality 3D datasets. However, as we observed, constrained by their matching-based principles, the reconstruction quality of existing models suffers significant degradation in challenging regions with limited matching cues, particularly in weakly textured areas and low-light conditions. To mitigate these limitations, we propose to harness the inherent robustness of monocular geometry estimation to compensate for the inherent shortcomings of matching-based methods. Specifically, we introduce a monocular-guided refinement module that integrates monocular geometric priors into multi-view reconstruction frameworks. This integration substantially enhances the robustness of multi-view reconstruction systems, leading to high-quality feed-forward reconstructions. Comprehensive experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves substantial improvements in both mutli-view camera pose estimation and point cloud accuracy.

2504.13157.title: AerialMegaDepth: Learning Aerial-Ground Reconstruction and View Synthesis

screening.reason: The main contribution is a hybrid dataset (AerialMegaDepth) combining pseudo-synthetic aerial renderings with real ground-level images, used to fine-tune existing models like DUSt3R for aerial-ground reconstruction. It is a resource directly useful for training core methods on a challenging viewpoint-change scenario, but it is domain-specific rather than targeting the general unposed reconstruction problem.
screening.evidence: we propose a scalable framework combining pseudo-synthetic renderings from 3D city-wide meshes (e.g., Google Earth) with real, ground-level crowd-sourced images (e.g., MegaDepth)
screening.task: aerial-ground geometric reconstruction and view synthesis

2504.13157.abstract: We explore the task of geometric reconstruction of images captured from a mixture of ground and aerial views. Current state-of-the-art learning-based approaches fail to handle the extreme viewpoint variation between aerial-ground image pairs. Our hypothesis is that the lack of high-quality, co-registered aerial-ground datasets for training is a key reason for this failure. Such data is difficult to assemble precisely because it is difficult to reconstruct in a scalable way. To overcome this challenge, we propose a scalable framework combining pseudo-synthetic renderings from 3D city-wide meshes (e.g., Google Earth) with real, ground-level crowd-sourced images (e.g., MegaDepth). The pseudo-synthetic data simulates a wide range of aerial viewpoints, while the real, crowd-sourced images help improve visual fidelity for ground-level images where mesh-based renderings lack sufficient detail, effectively bridging the domain gap between real images and pseudo-synthetic renderings. Using this hybrid dataset, we fine-tune several state-of-the-art algorithms and achieve significant improvements on real-world, zero-shot aerial-ground tasks. For example, we observe that baseline DUSt3R localizes fewer than 5% of aerial-ground pairs within 5 degrees of camera rotation error, while fine-tuning with our data raises accuracy to nearly 56%, addressing a major failure point in handling large viewpoint changes. Beyond camera estimation and scene reconstruction, our dataset also improves performance on downstream tasks like novel-view synthesis in challenging aerial-ground scenarios, demonstrating the practical value of our approach in real-world applications.

2504.01732.title: FIORD: A Fisheye Indoor-Outdoor Dataset with LIDAR Ground Truth for 3D Scene Reconstruction and Benchmarking

2504.01732.abstract: The development of large-scale 3D scene reconstruction and novel view synthesis methods mostly rely on datasets comprising perspective images with narrow fields of view (FoV). While effective for small-scale scenes, these datasets require large image sets and extensive structure-from-motion (SfM) processing, limiting scalability. To address this, we introduce a fisheye image dataset tailored for scene reconstruction tasks. Using dual 200-degree fisheye lenses, our dataset provides full 360-degree coverage of 5 indoor and 5 outdoor scenes. Each scene has sparse SfM point clouds and precise LIDAR-derived dense point clouds that can be used as geometric ground-truth, enabling robust benchmarking under challenging conditions such as occlusions and reflections. While the baseline experiments focus on vanilla Gaussian Splatting and NeRF based Nerfacto methods, the dataset supports diverse approaches for scene reconstruction, novel view synthesis, and image-based rendering.

2503.17856.title: ClaraVid: A Holistic Scene Reconstruction Benchmark From Aerial Perspective With Delentropy-Based Complexity Profiling

screening.reason: The paper introduces ClaraVid, a synthetic aerial dataset with dense depth and point clouds, and a complexity metric to benchmark neural reconstruction methods.
screening.evidence: We introduce ClaraVid, a synthetic aerial dataset specifically designed to overcome these limitations
screening.task: Aerial scene reconstruction benchmarking and complexity profiling

2503.17856.abstract: The development of aerial holistic scene understanding algorithms is hindered by the scarcity of comprehensive datasets that enable both semantic and geometric reconstruction. While synthetic datasets offer an alternative, existing options exhibit task-specific limitations, unrealistic scene compositions, and rendering artifacts that compromise real-world applicability. We introduce ClaraVid, a synthetic aerial dataset specifically designed to overcome these limitations. Comprising 16,917 high-resolution images captured at 4032x3024 from multiple viewpoints across diverse landscapes, ClaraVid provides dense depth maps, panoptic segmentation, sparse point clouds, and dynamic object masks, while mitigating common rendering artifacts. To further advance neural reconstruction, we introduce the Delentropic Scene Profile (DSP), a novel complexity metric derived from differential entropy analysis, designed to quantitatively assess scene difficulty and inform reconstruction tasks. Utilizing DSP, we systematically benchmark neural reconstruction methods, uncovering a consistent, measurable correlation between scene complexity and reconstruction accuracy. Empirical results indicate that higher delentropy strongly correlates with increased reconstruction errors, validating DSP as a reliable complexity prior. The data and code are available on the project page at https://rdbch.github.io/claravid/

2411.17605.title: Distractor-free Generalizable 3D Gaussian Splatting

screening.reason: DGGS is a feedforward generalizable 3DGS method that directly predicts 3D scene geometry from unposed reference images, qualifying as core; however, its main contribution is the distractor-free mechanism (mask prediction, reference scoring, pruning) rather than a new geometry prediction architecture, making it a narrower-scope core contribution.

screening.task: feedforward 3D Gaussian Splatting with distractor handling

2411.17605.abstract: We present DGGS, a novel framework that addresses the previously unexplored challenge: $\textbf{Distractor-free Generalizable 3D Gaussian Splatting}$ (3DGS). It mitigates 3D inconsistency and training instability caused by distractor data in the cross-scenes generalizable train setting while enabling feedforward inference for 3DGS and distractor masks from references in the unseen scenes. To achieve these objectives, DGGS proposes a scene-agnostic reference-based mask prediction and refinement module during the training phase, effectively eliminating the impact of distractor on training stability. Moreover, we combat distractor-induced artifacts and holes at inference time through a novel two-stage inference framework for references scoring and re-selection, complemented by a distractor pruning mechanism that further removes residual distractor 3DGS-primitive influences. Extensive feedforward experiments on the real and our synthetic data show DGGS's reconstruction capability when dealing with novel distractor scenes. Moreover, our generalizable mask prediction even achieves an accuracy superior to existing scene-specific training methods. Homepage is https://github.com/bbbbby-99/DGGS.
2411.17605.authors: Yanqi Bao, Jing Liao, Jing Huo, Yang Gao

2611.31140.title: HoloSplat: Real-Time Token Streaming for Feed-Forward Human Reconstruction

screening.reason: The main contribution is a real-time streaming codec (token pruning, PCA, geometry coding) applied to an existing feed-forward human reconstructor, not a new dense geometry prediction model. This is applying an existing core model to a different task (bandwidth-constrained streaming), which fits score 3 rather than 2 because the streaming framework is a substantive system contribution built directly on the core pipeline.
screening.evidence: splits a feed-forward reconstructor before its Gaussian head
screening.task: real-time streaming of human-centric volumetric video via compressed 3D Gaussian tokens

2611.31140.abstract: Live free-viewpoint video streaming of humans enables immersive telepresence and interactive XR applications. However, this requires reconstructing each frame in real time, transmitting the data within strict bandwidth budgets, and decoding it on lightweight client GPUs. Existing approaches, whether relying on per-frame optimization or feed-forward inference, generate massive 3D Gaussian payloads that exceed practical streaming limits, while aggressive compression severely degrades rendering quality. In this work, we present HoloSplat, a real-time streaming framework for human-centric volumetric video. HoloSplat splits a feed-forward reconstructor before its Gaussian head, introducing a multi-rate streaming codec driven by server-side token compression and client-side token restoration. On the server side, we apply opacity-guided token pruning, PCA-based dimensionality reduction, and lossless geometry coding for token anchors. On the client side, a feature reconstruction hypernetwork is fused into the Gaussian head to recover compression-induced quality loss. Furthermore, we introduce Neural Session Calibration (NSC), which rapidly fine-tunes the Gaussian head online using incoming camera views during a warm-up phase. This resolves quality degradation from novel camera parameters and varying capture conditions with zero per-frame overhead. In our evaluations, HoloSplat averages 32.2 FPS on four RTX 5090 GPUs at 50 Mbit/s. It decodes each frame into 3D Gaussians in 22.1 ms on an RTX 3050 Ti laptop GPU, transmitting 22.8$\times$ less data than uncompressed float32 Gaussians, while calibrated decoding improves PSNR by 1.050 dB.
2611.31140.authors: Chaofan Li, Qihan Ding, Shihan Wang, Zhehao Shen, Boyu Shen, Quanyu Chen, Haoyu Wu, Lan Xu, Xin Lou

2611.30173.abstract: Dense visual SLAM built on learned two-view geometry is evaluated in good light; in low light it fails silently. Two frames of 9-level quantized noise, no scene at all, give MASt3R-SLAM's network a cross-view geometric self-consistency of 0.936; a real dark frame pair gives 0.935. Starved of structure, the network invents the same geometry for both views and the system trusts the agreement: on a dark sequence it consumes 1,605 frames, emits 7 keyframes, rejects no factor-graph edges and reports full frame rate, while over 95% of the correspondences it accepts violate the ground-truth epipolar geometry. One inflated statistic is read by two subsystems against thresholds in opposite directions, so keyframing starves while relocalization accepts almost every candidate. The same statistic, read at keyframe-pair baselines, separates the confident collapse from working runs on the ETH3D dark sequences without ground truth or extra computation (in-sample). Low-light-adapted weights take tracked trajectories from 1/6 to 5/6, as does retuning two thresholds; neither yields accurate ones, because the adaptation withdraws confidence from wrong geometry rather than finding right geometry. Replayed on a Jetson AGX Orin carried by a legged robot, the mechanism's signature reproduces on the two darkest of four routes, and which of its faces appears varies with route geometry and sensor encoding. The network does not lose confidence in the dark; it manufactures it.

2611.25445.title: Stereo Visual Odometry with In-the-Loop Geometric Feed-Forward Models Towards Dense Metric Mapping

screening.reason: The paper integrates feed-forward geometry models as a component within a stereo visual odometry framework, with the main contribution being the factor-graph-based calibration and alignment system rather than a new geometry prediction model. This is a useful application of an existing core model to a different task (SVO and dense metric mapping).
screening.evidence: integrates geometric feed-forward models (GFMs) for dense depth prediction with factor-graph-based visual odometry
screening.task: stereo visual odometry and dense metric mapping

2611.25445.abstract: We present a stereo visual odometry (SVO) framework that integrates geometric feed-forward models (GFMs) for dense depth prediction with factor-graph-based visual odometry to achieve accurate localisation and dense metric mapping. Our key idea is to exploit sparse but reliable metric geometry estimated from stereo and temporal multi-view observations to calibrate dense GFM predictions, while retaining the robustness and efficiency of model-based SVO. Rather than directly conditioning the GFM on potentially noisy stereo depth, optimised 3D landmarks are used to jointly estimate a scale-shift transformation over all keyframes within each local submap, yielding metrically consistent dense depth predictions. To balance accuracy and computational efficiency, we introduce a hierarchical factor-graph architecture. At the local level, sliding-window optimisation estimates high-frequency camera poses and multi-view-refined 3D landmarks. Dense predictions are generated only for selected keyframes and registered within each submap using SE(3) Generalised ICP. Consecutive submaps are further aligned in Sim(3) using their shared geometry, allowing residual scale inconsistencies to be corrected. These intra- and inter-submap constraints are incorporated into a global factor graph to produce a consistent trajectory and dense metric reconstruction. Extensive experiments on public and in-house datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves competitive odometry accuracy against geometric and learning-based baselines while providing accurate dense metric reconstruction and improved robustness to failures in learned depth prediction.

2611.23554.title: Layer-Matched Sparse Attention for Low-Redundancy 3D Reconstruction

screening.reason: The paper proposes a training-free sparse attention mechanism to accelerate VGGT, which is an optimization-centered method applied to a core model rather than an independent geometry prediction contribution. The instructions explicitly classify optimization-centered methods that lack a core contribution as related.
screening.evidence: Training-free accelerators thin this attention and work well on redundant video
screening.task: efficient 3D reconstruction from unposed images via sparse attention

2611.23554.abstract: VGGT reconstructs cameras and geometry from unposed images in one pass, but its global attention grows quadratically with the number of views. Training-free accelerators thin this attention and work well on redundant video, but lose pose accuracy when views share little geometry. This paper traces these losses to two kinds of cross-view information that a uniform sparse approximation can fail to preserve together: diffuse layers aggregate distributed context, whereas matching layers depend on query-specific interactions that carry little attention mass. A per-layer statistic measures the log-mass missed by a mean token. Its row-free proxy is the logit variance, and it selects the estimator for each layer. Diffuse layers use shared, importance-sampled hub keys, with log-weights that make the softmax numerator and denominator unbiased. Matching layers stay exact: every aggressive thinning tested cost accuracy. At equal cost, the selected layers outperform the four shifted windows tested. On 13 unseen low-redundancy scenes with 32 views, LMSA stays within 1.4 AUC@5 of dense attention, compared with 10.3 for AVGGT and 4.5 for SAF3R; its difference from contemporaneous GPA-VGGT is not significant, and only its gains over AVGGT pass both scene-level tests. With 100 views, it stays within 1.9 AUC@5 while its aggregator runs $2.0\times$ faster. Used post hoc to choose the layers GPA-VGGT protects, the statistic improves it by 1.2 AUC@5 for 5% more FLOPs. Applied untuned to $π^3$, it beats AVGGT but remains further from dense accuracy.

2611.23051.title: Refin3R: Geometry-Guided Refinement for Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction

screening.reason: Refin3R is a refinement module that requires SfM points as a geometric prior input, positioning it as an auxiliary component on top of feed-forward point map models rather than a standalone model that reconstructs dense geometry from unposed images alone. It produces comparable outputs (dense point maps) but the dependency on SfM geometry as input places it in adjacent rather than core territory.
screening.evidence: refines feed-forward point maps with Structure-from-Motion (SfM) points
screening.task: refining feed-forward point maps using SfM geometry priors

2611.23051.abstract: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models predict dense point maps from multiple images in a single pass. Without explicit geometric constraints, however, their predictions are often inconsistent across views and lack fine-grained precision. Recent methods incorporate geometric priors such as camera pose or depth, but use them merely as auxiliary inputs, process each view independently, or refine the geometry only where the priors are available. We present Refin3R, which refines feed-forward point maps with Structure-from-Motion (SfM) points, propagating SfM geometry over the image grid. In its dual-branch architecture, a 2D branch extends SfM geometry beyond its coverage using geometry-aware backbone features, while a 3D branch reasons over the SfM points of all views, capturing multi-view structure that the image grid alone cannot represent. The two branches exchange information bidirectionally to jointly refine each view, yielding dense and accurate point maps. Across ScanNet++, ETH3D, Tanks\&Temples, and out-of-domain human and surgical scenes, Refin3R consistently outperforms feed-forward and geometry-guided methods in point map accuracy while running faster than the strongest geometry-guided baseline.
2611.23051.authors: Jongmin Lee, Jaeyeong Kim, Seungryong Kim

2611.22244.title: PhyVGGT: Feed-Forward Articulated Object Reconstruction from Monocular Videos

screening.reason: The paper applies a frozen 3D foundation model to articulated object reconstruction by adding task-specific decoder layers for part segmentation and joint estimation, making it a useful application of core geometry to a new task rather than a core geometry contribution itself. The base model is frozen and the main contribution is the downstream articulated reconstruction pipeline.
screening.evidence: a single-pass framework on a frozen 3D foundation model
screening.task: articulated object reconstruction from monocular video

2611.22244.abstract: Reconstructing an articulated object with its 3D movable parts, joint parameters and unseen articulation states from an uncalibrated monocular video is essential for robot manipulation and interactive digital twins. Existing per-scene optimisation methods require minutes to hours and external depth or camera poses, whereas feed-forward 3D foundation models reconstruct dense point maps in one pass without segmenting movable parts or inferring joints. Even on these monocular point maps, regressing or fitting continuous joints directly fails on casual videos, since cross-frame attention blurs moving part boundaries in deep layers, underestimates motion along the viewing ray and leaves continuous axes ill-conditioned under small opening angles. To address these challenges, we propose PhyVGGT, a single-pass framework on a frozen 3D foundation model that anchors moving-part matching and closed-form joint estimation to the undistorted geometry of the stationary base. First, our Part and Motion Decoder fuses intermediate per-frame tokens with global tokens and references part queries to a static-base query to segment 3D parts, align point maps on the static base and predict learned Bingham priors. Second, our Kinematic Inference Layer fits an orthogonal Manhattan frame to static surface normals, selects the joint axis in closed form under a Bingham posterior combining pairwise motion scatter with the learned priors, and solves a linear system for the hinge pivot to drive unseen states. Trained solely on synthetic data, PhyVGGT achieves state-of-the-art monocular performance across five benchmarks, outperforming FAMOS and monocular ArtiPoint, surpassing posed RGB-D ArtiPoint in median error, and running in 6.8 s per 48-frame video against hours of per-scene optimisation in Articulat3D. Project page: https://phyvggt.github.io.
2611.22244.authors: Qi Shao, Zhihao Cao, Shuhao Zhai, Anh Nguyen, Hong Liang, Baoru Huang, Liang Li

2611.18099.title: Eco3R: Pinned-Key Inference for Efficient and Streamable Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction from Long Videos

screening.reason: Eco3R is a training-free inference optimization framework for existing feed-forward 3D reconstruction models (VGGT, π³), not a new geometry prediction model itself. It is useful adjacent work that improves efficiency of core-task models but does not establish an independent core geometry contribution.
screening.evidence: a training-free inference framework whose keys form a Pinned Key Set of 31 such frames
screening.task: efficient feed-forward 3D reconstruction from long videos

2611.18099.abstract: Feed-forward multi-view transformers such as VGGT recover the cameras and geometry of a video in one pass, but the cost of their cross-frame self-attention grows quadratically with the frame count, and their accuracy drops on long videos. Most remedies approximate attention over all frames under a fixed computational budget or select a few keys by their content. We hypothesize that the keys of a long video can be selected independently of video content, and our experiments on VGGT and $π^3$ support it: a small number of uniformly sampled frames can serve as the keys of every frame. We present Eco3R, a training-free inference framework whose keys form a Pinned Key Set of 31 such frames. A pin pass stores their tokens in a Scene Cache, and the other frames read it in independent batches that reproduce joint inference with these keys exactly, at a constant cost per frame. An Online Stream updates the pinned frames during recording. Six middle global blocks align the frames and form a reusable VGGT module: the Alignment Score reads their attention to flag failures, and Alignment Refocusing reduces them by fine-tuning only these blocks (3.6 GPU hours). Eco3R ($π^3$) matches $π^3$'s success rate on 1,000-frame ScanNet videos while running 13.8 times faster. With refocusing, Eco3R (VGGT) raises VGGT's success rate from 70% to 82% while running 8.5 times faster on 500 frames. Eco3R can reconstruct sequences of up to 4,000 frames on a single A100 GPU, while Eco3R ($π^3$) streams 1,000 frames at 18.6 fps, achieving the lowest online absolute trajectory error.
2611.18099.authors: Hongsen Cao, Shanxin Yuan, Mona Jaber, Ahmed Sayed

2611.17629.title: Training-Free Acceleration of Multi-View 3D Transformers via Regime-Aware Attention Approximation

screening.reason: The model did not supply a matching quotation.
screening.task: inference acceleration of multi-view 3D transformers via attention approximation

2611.17629.abstract: Multi-view 3D transformers such as VGGT reconstruct a scene from a set of unposed images in a single forward pass, predicting camera poses, depth and 3D points, but the cost of their global attention grows quadratically with the num- ber of images. Accelerators borrowed from large language models assume that each token attends to only a few oth- ers; on these models they lose accuracy or gain little speed. We study the global attention of three multi-view transform- ers on seven datasets and find that every layer plays one of three roles: it averages over the whole scene, matches points across many images, or anchors on the first image, whose coordinates the outputs use. Building on this anal- ysis, we propose Regime-AWare ATTention Approximation (RAWATTA), a training-free method that runs attention in 8- bit precision and keeps 16-bit precision only in the layers where a worst-case calibration check requires it. Its fast set- ting, RAWATTA-Fast, also approximates attention in a few averaging and anchoring layers, while matching layers and the first image keep all their keys. On a 12 GB GPU at 50 im- ages, RAWATTA runs VGGT faster than the released code, mostly through our CUDA engine, and loses at most about one point of pose accuracy (AUC@3) on any dataset; RAWATTA-Fast is slightly faster and less accurate. Both fit 200 images, where the released code runs out of memory at 100.
2611.17629.authors: Muhammed Izzet Sezer, Sevval Belkis Dikkaya

2611.15435.title: ThermalSplat: Generalizable Pose-Free Gaussian Splatting for Sparse-View Thermal 3D Reconstruction

screening.reason: The model did not supply a matching quotation.
screening.task: pose-free 3D scene reconstruction from sparse thermal images

2611.15435.abstract: Thermal infrared imaging is vital for applications like search-and-rescue and autonomous navigation, yet trans- lating it into 3D scene representations remains a critical bottleneck. The low-texture nature and view-dependent emissivity of thermal images cause standard pose estima- tors to fail catastrophically, collapsing standard 3D Gaus- sian Splatting pipelines under sparse-view constraints. Fur- thermore, existing thermal reconstruction methods rely heavily on dense capture and computationally expensive per-scene optimization. Critically, many of these ap- proaches depend on aligned RGB-thermal datasets to ob- tain reliable camera poses and initial point clouds, ren- dering them unusable in purely thermal, unposed envi- ronments. To break this bottleneck, we present Thermal- Splat, the first generalizable, feed-forward Gaussian splat- ting framework that reconstructs 3D scenes directly from sparse thermal images without requiring known camera poses, RGB guidance, or per-scene training. We over- come thermal-specific challenges using a soft census loss for brightness-invariant structural matching and a bound- ary structure loss to explicitly supervise temperature discon- tinuities. Trained on an aggregated multi-source dataset, ThermalSplat synthesizes sharp reconstructions of unseen scenes in a single feed-forward pass. Extensive experi- ments demonstrate that ThermalSplat holds a strict advan- tage over scene-specific thermal splatting methods in the sparse regime. Furthermore, even compared against these baselines operating under their ideal dense capture set- tings, ThermalSplat achieves superior perceptual fidelity. By eliminating the need for computationally expensive per scene optimization, ThermalSplat offers an efficient and generalizable approach to thermal 3D reconstruction.
2611.15435.authors: Prasanna S, Gopi Raju Matta, Divya Madhuri Vemunuri, Kaushik Mitra

2611.15143.title: Multi-View 3D Reconstruction Using V-JEPA Features

screening.reason: The paper performs multi-view 3D reconstruction with pointmaps from unposed RGB images, placing it in the same task space as DUSt3R, but its main contribution is studying whether V-JEPA video-pretrained features improve reconstruction, with largely mixed or negative results rather than a new core model or substantive architectural extension. Score 4 is less appropriate because the paper does not propose a new reconstruction architecture or demonstrate a clear improvement over existing core methods.
screening.evidence: residual pointmaps
screening.task: multi-view 3D reconstruction from unposed RGB images

2611.15143.abstract: Predictive video encoders provide dense visual representations, but adapting them to 3D reconstruction requires accurate depth, camera poses, and cross-view geometry. We study supervised RGB-only multi-view reconstruction using an architecture that combines video-pretrained features, camera estimation, scene aggregation, epipolar transport, and residual pointmaps. Experiments compare global and spatial camera regression with joint relative objectives on CO3D, alongside an independently trained TUM RGB-D model. On 168 CO3D five-view windows, the spatial-camera configuration achieves 29.3% lower absolute trajectory error than the global-camera configuration, but performs worse than identity poses in trajectory error and worse than the global configuration in depth error. The joint relative-objective configuration improves normalized intrinsics error and similarity-aligned Chamfer distance from 0.6447 to 0.5573, but increases raw Chamfer distance from 3.5535 to 4.4374. On 163 indoor windows, camera error is 0.3063 m versus 0.3694 m for identity poses, while depth error is 0.4279 versus 0.2516 for constant median depth. Refinement worsens indoor camera error, and additional experiments show competing depth and pose effects. Overall, the results distinguish representation adaptation, aligned shape, and raw reconstruction, highlighting the need for isolated component and encoder comparisons before attributing reconstruction gains to predictive video pretraining.

2611.14440.title: UGG: Unified Generative Geometry Model

screening.reason: UGG is a generative (diffusion-based) model that jointly predicts depth, camera pose, and video, addressing the same geometry-from-images task as DUSt3R but with a fundamentally different generative formulation rather than feedforward pointmap prediction. The abstract explicitly contrasts feedforward geometric prediction with generative synthesis, positioning UGG as a unification of both rather than a direct extension of DUSt3R's architecture.
screening.evidence: formulates visual generation and geometric prediction as conditional completion within a single generative model
screening.task: unified 4D scene understanding: depth estimation, camera pose prediction, and camera-controlled video generation

2611.14440.abstract: Understanding 4D scenes is a core challenge in visual intelligence, requiring models to jointly capture scene geometry, appearance, and dynamics from partial observations. However, existing approaches are subdivided into feedforward models for direct geometric prediction, and generative models for visual synthesis. We introduce UGG, a unified framework for 4D scene understanding that jointly models RGB video and geometric representations such as depth and camera pose. By assigning different noise levels across modalities and time, UGG formulates visual generation and geometric prediction as conditional completion within a single generative model. This flexible formulation enables the model to learn from diverse, heterogeneous datasets with different subsets of geometric and visual annotations. Furthermore, our generative formulation enables inference-time search over multiple plausible scene hypotheses, using geometric evidence extracted from observed RGB frames to improve geometric prediction without ground truth geometry. We demonstrate UGG's effectiveness over non-unified baselines across camera-controlled video generation, depth estimation, and camera pose prediction, including in challenging sparse observation settings. Code and visualizations are available at https://ugg-model.github.io/

2611.13453.abstract: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction (3R) from unconstrained multi-view images has recently emerged as a prominent research direction in 3D computer vision. Various foundational reconstruction models have been proposed with different architectures and reconstruction paradigms. Despite being trained on large-scale perspective datasets with substantial computational resources, these models generally struggle to generalize to non-perspective images. This limitation hinders their deployment in applications involving arbitrary, unknown, and potentially heterogeneous camera models. To build on the capabilities of existing reconstruction models with minimal retraining, we propose Camera3R, a low-rank adaptation framework that efficiently extends perspective-pretrained 3R networks to any other camera models. Extensive experiments demonstrate that, with only 0.5% additional parameters and less than a day of training, Camera3R adapts a foundational 3D reconstruction model to non-perspective cameras while fully preserving its original performance on perspective inputs. Code is available at https://github.com/android-xr/camera3r.

2611.11964.title: 3R-Adapter: Retrieval, Rewiring, and Refinement for Efficient Adaptation of 3D Reconstruction Model

screening.reason: The paper proposes a PEFT adaptation method for existing feed-forward 3D reconstruction models in long-tail scenarios, not a new reconstruction model or extension of DUSt3R's architecture or pointmaps. It is useful adjacent work that improves existing core models but does not itself contribute a core geometry prediction model.
screening.evidence: a PEFT paradigm for long-tail 3D reconstruction scenarios
screening.task: parameter-efficient adaptation of 3D reconstruction models for long-tail scenarios

2611.11964.abstract: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models have demonstrated strong generalization under large-scale pre-training, yet they struggle in long-tail scenarios such as low-light reconstruction, joint human-scene reconstruction, and test-time adaptation. We observe relational attention structure collapse, manifested as the failure of cross-view correspondences, as a primary cause of these limitations. While adaptation offers a practical way to bridge this gap, existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) approaches mainly perform channel-wise feature adjustment and lack mechanisms to explicitly adapt relational structures, leaving correspondence failures unresolved. In this work, we formulate adaptation of 3D reconstruction models as a problem of correspondence recovery under domain shift and propose 3R-Adapter, a PEFT paradigm for long-tail 3D reconstruction scenarios. Our method consists of three components: Deformable Retrieval for task-adaptive relation candidate retrieval, Relational Rewiring for reconstructing cross-view relational structures, and Consistency Refinement for injecting the rewired relations into stable predictions. Extensive experiments on low-light reconstruction, joint human-scene reconstruction, and test-time adaptation demonstrate that our approach significantly improves robustness over existing PEFT methods while maintaining efficient lightweight adaptation. Our code is released at https://github.com/PKU-OV3-LAB/3R-Adapter.
2611.11964.authors: Zixiang Ai, Zhenyu Cui, Xu Zou, Jiahuan Zhou

2611.08436.title: SM4RT: Cascaded Feed-forward Model for 4D Reconstruction

screening.reason: SM4RT is a feed-forward model that predicts 3D geometry from unposed RGB video, which is relevant to the DUSt3R survey, but its main contribution is the cascade framework for 4D reconstruction with motion estimation as the primary novelty rather than the geometry prediction itself. The geometry component is described as competitive rather than state-of-the-art, making it a useful adjacent work rather than a core geometry contribution.

screening.task: 4D reconstruction (geometry + motion estimation) from RGB video

2611.08436.abstract: We introduce SM4RT, a multi-task cascade feed-forward model for dynamic scene reconstruction from RGB videos. While existing feed-forward approaches typically address geometry reconstruction and motion estimation separately--and often predict motions in a single coordinate frame that must account for camera movement--SM4RT solves these tasks sequentially by first reconstructing 3D geometry and then bootstrapping motion estimation from the predicted structure. By expressing each pixel's 3D motion in its corresponding camera frame, SM4RT reduces ambiguity arising from camera motion. To address the sparsity of real-world motion labels, SM4RT further incorporates a weakly supervised loss that regularizes unlabeled point motions using labeled point positions at the other time step. We additionally benchmark geometry reconstruction on five dynamic scene datasets and show that SM4RT achieves competitive performance with state-of-the-art methods. Overall, our unified framework demonstrates that combining geometry reconstruction and motion estimation in a cascade not only avoids performance trade-offs but also enhances motion estimation through improved geometric reasoning.

For loop closure, neighboring image pairs support a consistency check and translation-scale alignment. Each accepted candidate contributes one robust Sim(3) factor between existing center-frame nodes, without an auxiliary loop submap. A 17-sequence comparison lowers mean Sim(3) ATE on nine TUM sequences from 0.1018 to 0.0451 m relative to the VGGT-SLAM 2.0 baseline. Anchoring improves all seven no-loop module ablations. 2611.06258.title: CrossPressor: Scalable Cross-View Fusion for Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting

2611.06258.abstract: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3D-GS) becomes increasingly difficult to scale to long multi-view sequences. Anchor-based compression methods such as ZPressor alleviate representation growth by decoding Gaussians only from a compact set of anchor feature maps, but keeping these anchors fixed forces each one to aggregate an increasing number of support views. We identify this representation--fusion mismatch and introduce \textbf{CrossPressor}, a training-free method for scalable anchor-based fusion. CrossPressor preserves all decoder-facing anchor queries while constraining the view-growing support sequence through coverage-cycled evidence routing, distributing retained spatial evidence across support views and fusion layers while keeping all support views represented. Routing before K/V projection, together with joint context packing, further reduces support-side fusion cost without retraining. CrossPressor maintains reconstruction quality close to dense fusion while achieving up to $26.12\times$ faster cross-view fusion and $1.43\times$ end-to-end acceleration on long input sequences. Our project page is at: https://yuhsihu.github.io/CrossPressor.

Specifically, we propose a simple yet effective pipeline that constructs multi-view-consistent segmentation pseudo-labels through image cropping and geometric transformations. We further introduce a lightweight, plug-and-play network that leverages the multi-view-consistent image features learned by existing pretrained 3D foundation models and the generated pseudo-labels to perform multi-view-consistent segmentation. Importantly, our flexible framework supports various types of prompts provided from one or multiple views and can be readily extended to open-vocabulary 3D segmentation. Under this single-image supervision, our feed-forward model achieves the best mIoU on NVOS, remains competitive on SPIn-NeRF and ScanNet++ against baselines using per-scene optimization or in-domain multi-view training, and demonstrates zero-shot transfer to open-vocabulary 3D segmentation. 2611.04025.abstract: State-of-the-art bronchoscopy guidance systems and computer-aided diagnosis methods have emerged as important tools for early lung cancer detection. Effective use of these tools depends on being able to accurately link a patient's bronchoscopic airway exam video to their pre-operative 3D chest CT scan. Unfortunately, the derivation of such links, which include bronchoscope depth and camera motion, from the exam video remains an open problem. Building on recently proposed 3D-vision foundation models, we propose DUNEDepth, a hybrid architecture that combines a shared DUNE ViT encoder, a twin MASt3R cross-attention decoder structure, and a prediction head that includes elements of the MASt3R and Reloc3r models. To fine-tune the architecture to our application, we utilize an integrated hybrid synthetic-supervised/self-supervised training strategy that draws on both bronchoscopic video and CT-derived virtual bronchoscopic views. Experiments drawing on bronchoscopic video sequences demonstrate that DUNEDepth more accurately derives depth information and camera motion trajectories than previously proposed self-supervised methods.
