screening.task: 3D semantic field construction and open-vocabulary querying from sparse views

2412.08331.abstract: 3D semantic field learning is crucial for applications like autonomous navigation, AR/VR, and robotics, where accurate comprehension of 3D scenes from limited viewpoints is essential. Existing methods struggle under sparse view conditions, relying on inefficient per-scene multi-view optimizations, which are impractical for many real-world tasks. To address this, we propose SLGaussian, a feed-forward method for constructing 3D semantic fields from sparse viewpoints, allowing direct inference of 3DGS-based scenes. By ensuring consistent SAM segmentations through video tracking and using low-dimensional indexing for high-dimensional CLIP features, SLGaussian efficiently embeds language information in 3D space, offering a robust solution for accurate 3D scene understanding under sparse view conditions. In experiments on two-view sparse 3D object querying and segmentation in the LERF and 3D-OVS datasets, SLGaussian outperforms existing methods in chosen IoU, Localization Accuracy, and mIoU. Moreover, our model achieves scene inference in under 30 seconds and open-vocabulary querying in just 0.011 seconds per query.

2412.06234.title: Generative Densification: Learning to Densify Gaussians for High-Fidelity Generalizable 3D Reconstruction

screening.reason: The paper proposes a densification module that enhances existing feed-forward Gaussian reconstruction models, but its core contribution is a post-processing enhancement rather than a standalone model that directly predicts dense geometry from unposed images. It is adjacent to the DUSt3R survey as it operates in the feed-forward 3D reconstruction space but does not extend DUSt3R's pointmap approach or constitute a comparable standalone reconstruction model.
screening.evidence: our method up-samples feature representations from the feed-forward models and generates their corresponding fine Gaussians in a single forward pass
screening.task: densifying Gaussians from feed-forward 3D reconstruction models

2412.06234.abstract: Generalized feed-forward Gaussian models have achieved significant progress in sparse-view 3D reconstruction by leveraging prior knowledge from large multi-view datasets. However, these models often struggle to represent high-frequency details due to the limited number of Gaussians. While the densification strategy used in per-scene 3D Gaussian splatting (3D-GS) optimization can be adapted to the feed-forward models, it may not be ideally suited for generalized scenarios. In this paper, we propose Generative Densification, an efficient and generalizable method to densify Gaussians generated by feed-forward models. Unlike the 3D-GS densification strategy, which iteratively splits and clones raw Gaussian parameters, our method up-samples feature representations from the feed-forward models and generates their corresponding fine Gaussians in a single forward pass, leveraging the embedded prior knowledge for enhanced generalization. Experimental results on both object-level and scene-level reconstruction tasks demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches with comparable or smaller model sizes, achieving notable improvements in representing fine details.
2412.06234.authors: Seungtae Nam, Xiangyu Sun, Gyeongjin Kang, Younggeun Lee, Seungjun Oh, Eunbyung Park

2412.04464.title: DualPM: Dual Posed-Canonical Point Maps for 3D Shape and Pose Reconstruction

screening.reason: The paper explicitly positions itself as developing an analogous point map concept for a very different problem (deformable object shape and pose with posed inputs), making it adjacent to DUSt3R's core unposed static scene reconstruction task rather than a direct extension of it.
screening.evidence: we develop an analogous concept for a very different problem
screening.task: 3D shape and pose reconstruction of deformable objects

2412.04464.abstract: The choice of data representation is a key factor in the success of deep learning in geometric tasks. For instance, DUSt3R recently introduced the concept of viewpoint-invariant point maps, generalizing depth prediction and showing that all key problems in the 3D reconstruction of static scenes can be reduced to predicting such point maps. In this paper, we develop an analogous concept for a very different problem: the reconstruction of the 3D shape and pose of deformable objects. To this end, we introduce Dual Point Maps (DualPM), where a pair of point maps is extracted from the same image-one associating pixels to their 3D locations on the object and the other to a canonical version of the object in its rest pose. We also extend point maps to amodal reconstruction to recover the complete shape of the object, even through self-occlusions. We show that 3D reconstruction and 3D pose estimation can be reduced to the prediction of DualPMs. Empirically, we demonstrate that this representation is a suitable target for deep networks to predict. Specifically, we focus on modeling quadrupeds, showing that DualPMs can be trained purely on synthetic 3D data, consisting of one or two models per category, while generalizing effectively to real images. With this approach, we achieve significant improvements over previous methods for the 3D analysis and reconstruction of such objects.
2412.04464.authors: Ben Kaye, Tomas Jakab, Shangzhe Wu, Christian Rupprecht, Andrea Vedaldi

2412.03079.title: Align3R: Aligned Monocular Depth Estimation for Dynamic Videos

screening.reason: The paper fine-tunes DUSt3R with additional monocular depth inputs and applies optimization to reconstruct depth and poses for dynamic videos, but the main contribution is the overall video-depth pipeline rather than a substantive extension of DUSt3R's model or pointmap geometry. screening.task: temporally consistent monocular video depth estimation for dynamic scenes

2412.03079.abstract: Recent developments in monocular depth estimation methods enable high-quality depth estimation of single-view images but fail to estimate consistent video depth across different frames. Recent works address this problem by applying a video diffusion model to generate video depth conditioned on the input video, which is training-expensive and can only produce scale-invariant depth values without camera poses. In this paper, we propose a novel video-depth estimation method called Align3R to estimate temporal consistent depth maps for a dynamic video. Our key idea is to utilize the recent DUSt3R model to align estimated monocular depth maps of different timesteps. First, we fine-tune the DUSt3R model with additional estimated monocular depth as inputs for the dynamic scenes. Then, we apply optimization to reconstruct both depth maps and camera poses. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Align3R estimates consistent video depth and camera poses for a monocular video with superior performance than baseline methods.

2412.02039.title: Multi-View 3D Reconstruction using Knowledge Distillation

screening.reason: The paper proposes a knowledge distillation pipeline that uses DUSt3R as a teacher to train smaller student models for 3D point prediction, which is an application of DUSt3R for efficiency rather than a substantive extension of its model or pointmap-based geometry. A core score would require a new geometry prediction contribution or model extension, which is absent here.

2412.02039.abstract: Large Foundation Models like Dust3r can produce high quality outputs such as pointmaps, camera intrinsics, and depth estimation, given stereo-image pairs as input. However, the application of these outputs on tasks like Visual Localization requires a large amount of inference time and compute resources. To address these limitations, in this paper, we propose the use of a knowledge distillation pipeline, where we aim to build a student-teacher model with Dust3r as the teacher and explore multiple architectures of student models that are trained using the 3D reconstructed points output by Dust3r. Our goal is to build student models that can learn scene-specific representations and output 3D points with replicable performance such as Dust3r. The data set we used to train our models is 12Scenes. We test two main architectures of models: a CNN-based architecture and a Vision Transformer based architecture. For each architecture, we also compare the use of pre-trained models against models built from scratch. We qualitatively compare the reconstructed 3D points output by the student model against Dust3r's and discuss the various features learned by the student model. We also perform ablation studies on the models through hyperparameter tuning. Overall, we observe that the Vision Transformer presents the best performance visually and quantitatively.
2412.02039.authors: Aditya Dutt, Ishikaa Lunawat, Manpreet Kaur

2411.17772.title: MVBoost: Boost 3D Reconstruction with Multi-View Refinement

screening.reason: The model did not supply a matching quotation.
screening.task: data augmentation for 3D object reconstruction via multi-view generation and refinement

2411.17772.abstract: Recent advancements in 3D object reconstruction have been remarkable, yet most current 3D models rely heavily on existing 3D datasets. The scarcity of diverse 3D datasets results in limited generalization capabilities of 3D reconstruction models. In this paper, we propose a novel framework for boosting 3D reconstruction with multi-view refinement (MVBoost) by generating pseudo-GT data. The key of MVBoost is combining the advantages of the high accuracy of the multi-view generation model and the consistency of the 3D reconstruction model to create a reliable data source. Specifically, given a single-view input image, we employ a multi-view diffusion model to generate multiple views, followed by a large 3D reconstruction model to produce consistent 3D data. MVBoost then adaptively refines these multi-view images, rendered from the consistent 3D data, to build a large-scale multi-view dataset for training a feed-forward 3D reconstruction model. Additionally, the input view optimization is designed to optimize the corresponding viewpoints based on the user's input image, ensuring that the most important viewpoint is accurately tailored to the user's needs. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that our method achieves superior reconstruction results and robust generalization compared to prior works.
2411.17772.authors: Xiangyu Liu, Xiaomei Zhang, Zhiyuan Ma, Xiangyu Zhu, Zhen Lei

screening.reason: NovelGS reconstructs 3D Gaussians from unposed images (the same task as core methods) but uses a diffusion-based iterative denoising approach rather than direct feed-forward prediction, making it adjacent work rather than a core contribution in the DUSt3R paradigm. 2411.16779.abstract: We introduce NovelGS, a diffusion model for Gaussian Splatting (GS) given sparse-view images. Recent works leverage feed-forward networks to generate pixel-aligned Gaussians, which could be fast rendered. Unfortunately, the method was unable to produce satisfactory results for areas not covered by the input images due to the formulation of these methods. In contrast, we leverage the novel view denoising through a transformer-based network to generate 3D Gaussians. Specifically, by incorporating both conditional views and noisy target views, the network predicts pixel-aligned Gaussians for each view. During training, the rendered target and some additional views of the Gaussians are supervised. During inference, the target views are iteratively rendered and denoised from pure noise. Our approach demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in addressing the multi-view image reconstruction challenge. Due to generative modeling of unseen regions, NovelGS effectively reconstructs 3D objects with consistent and sharp textures. Experimental results on publicly available datasets indicate that NovelGS substantially surpasses existing image-to-3D frameworks, both qualitatively and quantitatively. We also demonstrate the potential of NovelGS in generative tasks, such as text-to-3D and image-to-3D, by integrating it with existing multiview diffusion models. We will make the code publicly accessible.

2411.15966.title: Gaussian Scenes: Pose-Free Sparse-View Scene Reconstruction using Depth-Enhanced Diffusion Priors

screening.reason: The paper targets the same pose-free reconstruction task as DUSt3R but its core contribution is a generative/diffusion prior for view inpainting within an iterative Gaussian-SLAM loop, not a direct forward-pass prediction of dense geometry from unposed images. 2411.15966.abstract: In this work, we introduce a generative approach for pose-free (without camera parameters) reconstruction of 360 scenes from a sparse set of 2D images. Pose-free scene reconstruction from incomplete, pose-free observations is usually regularized with depth estimation or 3D foundational priors. While recent advances have enabled sparse-view reconstruction of large complex scenes (with high degree of foreground and background detail) with known camera poses using view-conditioned generative priors, these methods cannot be directly adapted for the pose-free setting when ground-truth poses are not available during evaluation. To address this, we propose an image-to-image generative model designed to inpaint missing details and remove artifacts in novel view renders and depth maps of a 3D scene. We introduce context and geometry conditioning using Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) modulation layers as a lightweight alternative to cross-attention and also propose a novel confidence measure for 3D Gaussian splat representations to allow for better detection of these artifacts. By progressively integrating these novel views in a Gaussian-SLAM-inspired process, we achieve a multi-view-consistent 3D representation. Evaluations on the MipNeRF360 and DL3DV-10K benchmark dataset demonstrate that our method surpasses existing pose-free techniques and performs competitively with state-of-the-art posed (precomputed camera parameters are given) reconstruction methods in complex 360 scenes. Our project page provides additional results, videos, and code.
2411.15966.authors: Soumava Paul, Prakhar Kaushik, Alan Yuille

2411.12309.title: DGTR: Distributed Gaussian Turbo-Reconstruction for Sparse-View Vast Scenes

screening.reason: The main contribution is a distributed framework for vast scene reconstruction using a feed-forward Gaussian model, not a new core geometry model itself. It applies an existing or unspecified feed-forward Gaussian predictor in a distributed setting with global alignment and distillation-based aggregation, making it useful adjacent work rather than a core model contribution.
screening.evidence: Using a feed-forward Gaussian model, we predict high-quality Gaussian primitives, followed by a global alignment algorithm to ensure geometric consistency
screening.task: distributed Gaussian reconstruction for sparse-view vast scenes

2411.12309.abstract: Novel-view synthesis (NVS) approaches play a critical role in vast scene reconstruction. However, these methods rely heavily on dense image inputs and prolonged training times, making them unsuitable where computational resources are limited. Additionally, few-shot methods often struggle with poor reconstruction quality in vast environments. This paper presents DGTR, a novel distributed framework for efficient Gaussian reconstruction for sparse-view vast scenes. Our approach divides the scene into regions, processed independently by drones with sparse image inputs. Using a feed-forward Gaussian model, we predict high-quality Gaussian primitives, followed by a global alignment algorithm to ensure geometric consistency. Synthetic views and depth priors are incorporated to further enhance training, while a distillation-based model aggregation mechanism enables efficient reconstruction. Our method achieves high-quality large-scale scene reconstruction and novel-view synthesis in significantly reduced training times, outperforming existing approaches in both speed and scalability. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework on vast aerial scenes, achieving high-quality results within minutes. Code will released on our [https://3d-aigc.github.io/DGTR].
2411.12309.authors: Hao Li, Yuanyuan Gao, Haosong Peng, Chenming Wu, Weicai Ye, Yufeng Zhan, Chen Zhao, Dingwen Zhang, Jingdong Wang, Junwei Han

2411.09145.title: Self-Supervised Monocular 4D Scene Reconstruction for Egocentric Videos

screening.reason: EgoMono4D performs feed-forward depth and pose estimation from unposed egocentric video frames, which is comparable to DUSt3R's task, but it is domain-specific to egocentric videos and builds on a pretrained single-frame depth model rather than extending DUSt3R's architecture, making it adjacent rather than a core contribution.
screening.evidence: unifies the estimation of multiple variables necessary for Egocentric Monocular 4D reconstruction, including camera intrinsic, camera poses, and video depth, all within a fast feed-forward framework
screening.task: self-supervised monocular 4D scene reconstruction from egocentric videos

2411.09145.abstract: Egocentric videos provide valuable insights into human interactions with the physical world, which has sparked growing interest in the computer vision and robotics communities. A critical challenge in fully understanding the geometry and dynamics of egocentric videos is dense scene reconstruction. However, the lack of high-quality labeled datasets in this field has hindered the effectiveness of current supervised learning methods. In this work, we aim to address this issue by exploring an self-supervised dynamic scene reconstruction approach. We introduce EgoMono4D, a novel model that unifies the estimation of multiple variables necessary for Egocentric Monocular 4D reconstruction, including camera intrinsic, camera poses, and video depth, all within a fast feed-forward framework. Starting from pretrained single-frame depth and intrinsic estimation model, we extend it with camera poses estimation and align multi-frame results on large-scale unlabeled egocentric videos. We evaluate EgoMono4D in both in-domain and zero-shot generalization settings, achieving superior performance in dense pointclouds sequence reconstruction compared to all baselines. EgoMono4D represents the first attempt to apply self-supervised learning for pointclouds sequence reconstruction to the label-scarce egocentric field, enabling fast, dense, and generalizable reconstruction. The interactable visualization, code and trained models are released https://egomono4d.github.io/
2411.09145.authors: Chengbo Yuan, Geng Chen, Li Yi, Yang Gao

2410.24207.title: No Pose, No Problem: Surprisingly Simple 3D Gaussian Splats from Sparse Unposed Images

screening.reason: The model did not supply a matching quotation.
screening.task: 3D scene reconstruction from unposed images

2410.24207.abstract: We introduce NoPoSplat, a feed-forward model capable of reconstructing 3D scenes parameterized by 3D Gaussians from \textit{unposed} sparse multi-view images. Our model, trained exclusively with photometric loss, achieves real-time 3D Gaussian reconstruction during inference. To eliminate the need for accurate pose input during reconstruction, we anchor one input view's local camera coordinates as the canonical space and train the network to predict Gaussian primitives for all views within this space. This approach obviates the need to transform Gaussian primitives from local coordinates into a global coordinate system, thus avoiding errors associated with per-frame Gaussians and pose estimation. To resolve scale ambiguity, we design and compare various intrinsic embedding methods, ultimately opting to convert camera intrinsics into a token embedding and concatenate it with image tokens as input to the model, enabling accurate scene scale prediction. We utilize the reconstructed 3D Gaussians for novel view synthesis and pose estimation tasks and propose a two-stage coarse-to-fine pipeline for accurate pose estimation. Experimental results demonstrate that our pose-free approach can achieve superior novel view synthesis quality compared to pose-required methods, particularly in scenarios with limited input image overlap. For pose estimation, our method, trained without ground truth depth or explicit matching loss, significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art methods with substantial improvements. This work makes significant advances in pose-free generalizable 3D reconstruction and demonstrates its applicability to real-world scenarios. Code and trained models are available at https://noposplat.github.io/.
2410.24207.authors: Botao Ye, Sifei Liu, Haofei Xu, Xueting Li, Marc Pollefeys, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Songyou Peng

2410.18956.title: Large Spatial Model: End-to-end Unposed Images to Semantic 3D

screening.reason: The model did not supply a matching quotation.
screening.task: End-to-end unposed image to semantic 3D reconstruction (geometry, appearance, semantics)

2410.18956.abstract: Reconstructing and understanding 3D structures from a limited number of images is a well-established problem in computer vision. Traditional methods usually break this task into multiple subtasks, each requiring complex transformations between different data representations. For instance, dense reconstruction through Structure-from-Motion (SfM) involves converting images into key points, optimizing camera parameters, and estimating structures. Afterward, accurate sparse reconstructions are required for further dense modeling, which is subsequently fed into task-specific neural networks. This multi-step process results in considerable processing time and increased engineering complexity. In this work, we present the Large Spatial Model (LSM), which processes unposed RGB images directly into semantic radiance fields. LSM simultaneously estimates geometry, appearance, and semantics in a single feed-forward operation, and it can generate versatile label maps by interacting with language at novel viewpoints. Leveraging a Transformer-based architecture, LSM integrates global geometry through pixel-aligned point maps. To enhance spatial attribute regression, we incorporate local context aggregation with multi-scale fusion, improving the accuracy of fine local details. To tackle the scarcity of labeled 3D semantic data and enable natural language-driven scene manipulation, we incorporate a pre-trained 2D language-based segmentation model into a 3D-consistent semantic feature field. An efficient decoder then parameterizes a set of semantic anisotropic Gaussians, facilitating supervised end-to-end learning. Extensive experiments across various tasks show that LSM unifies multiple 3D vision tasks directly from unposed images, achieving real-time semantic 3D reconstruction for the first time.

2409.19152.title: MASt3R-SfM: a Fully-Integrated Solution for Unconstrained Structure-from-Motion

screening.reason: The paper uses MASt3R as an off-the-shelf component for local 3D reconstructions and matches, with the main contribution being a novel SfM pipeline that adds global alignment and image retrieval. This is applying an existing core model to the SfM task rather than introducing a new geometry prediction model or architecture.
screening.evidence: build upon a recently released foundation model for 3D vision that can robustly produce local 3D reconstructions and accurate matches
screening.task: Structure-from-Motion: recovering camera poses and 3D geometry from unposed images

2409.19152.abstract: Structure-from-Motion (SfM), a task aiming at jointly recovering camera poses and 3D geometry of a scene given a set of images, remains a hard problem with still many open challenges despite decades of significant progress. The traditional solution for SfM consists of a complex pipeline of minimal solvers which tends to propagate errors and fails when images do not sufficiently overlap, have too little motion, etc. Recent methods have attempted to revisit this paradigm, but we empirically show that they fall short of fixing these core issues. In this paper, we propose instead to build upon a recently released foundation model for 3D vision that can robustly produce local 3D reconstructions and accurate matches. We introduce a low-memory approach to accurately align these local reconstructions in a global coordinate system. We further show that such foundation models can serve as efficient image retrievers without any overhead, reducing the overall complexity from quadratic to linear. Overall, our novel SfM pipeline is simple, scalable, fast and truly unconstrained, i.e. it can handle any collection of images, ordered or not. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks show that our method provides steady performance across diverse settings, especially outperforming existing methods in small- and medium-scale settings.
2409.19152.authors: Bardienus Duisterhof, Lojze Zust, Philippe Weinzaepfel, Vincent Leroy, Yohann Cabon, Jerome Revaud

2409.12753.title: DrivingForward: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting for Driving Scene Reconstruction from Flexible Surround-view Input

screening.reason: The paper proposes a feed-forward method that predicts 3D Gaussians from unposed images (the core task), but it is specifically designed for driving scenes with surround-view cameras, making it a domain-specific application rather than a general reconstruction contribution. The closest alternative score of 4 is less appropriate because the method is not a general-purpose extension of DUSt3R or a novel general reconstruction approach.
screening.evidence: reconstructs driving scenes from flexible surround-view input
screening.task: feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction of driving scenes from surround-view images

2409.12753.abstract: We propose DrivingForward, a feed-forward Gaussian Splatting model that reconstructs driving scenes from flexible surround-view input. Driving scene images from vehicle-mounted cameras are typically sparse, with limited overlap, and the movement of the vehicle further complicates the acquisition of camera extrinsics. To tackle these challenges and achieve real-time reconstruction, we jointly train a pose network, a depth network, and a Gaussian network to predict the Gaussian primitives that represent the driving scenes. The pose network and depth network determine the position of the Gaussian primitives in a self-supervised manner, without using depth ground truth and camera extrinsics during training. The Gaussian network independently predicts primitive parameters from each input image, including covariance, opacity, and spherical harmonics coefficients. At the inference stage, our model can achieve feed-forward reconstruction from flexible multi-frame surround-view input. Experiments on the nuScenes dataset show that our model outperforms existing state-of-the-art feed-forward and scene-optimized reconstruction methods in terms of reconstruction.
2409.12753.authors: Qijian Tian, Xin Tan, Yuan Xie, Lizhuang Ma

2409.08207.title: VI3DRM:Towards meticulous 3D Reconstruction from Sparse Views via Photo-Realistic Novel View Synthesis

screening.reason: The main contribution is a diffusion-based novel view synthesis model in a disentangled 3D latent space; pointmap construction is a downstream step leveraging the generated views rather than a direct geometry prediction model. This makes it useful adjacent work rather than a core geometry prediction contribution.
screening.evidence: our approach enables the accurate construction of pointmaps, ultimately producing finely textured meshes or point clouds
screening.task: sparse-view 3D reconstruction via novel view synthesis

2409.08207.abstract: Recently, methods like Zero-1-2-3 have focused on single-view based 3D reconstruction and have achieved remarkable success. However, their predictions for unseen areas heavily rely on the inductive bias of large-scale pretrained diffusion models. Although subsequent work, such as DreamComposer, attempts to make predictions more controllable by incorporating additional views, the results remain unrealistic due to feature entanglement in the vanilla latent space, including factors such as lighting, material, and structure. To address these issues, we introduce the Visual Isotropy 3D Reconstruction Model (VI3DRM), a diffusion-based sparse views 3D reconstruction model that operates within an ID consistent and perspective-disentangled 3D latent space. By facilitating the disentanglement of semantic information, color, material properties and lighting, VI3DRM is capable of generating highly realistic images that are indistinguishable from real photographs. By leveraging both real and synthesized images, our approach enables the accurate construction of pointmaps, ultimately producing finely textured meshes or point clouds. On the NVS task, tested on the GSO dataset, VI3DRM significantly outperforms state-of-the-art method DreamComposer, achieving a PSNR of 38.61, an SSIM of 0.929, and an LPIPS of 0.027. Code will be made available upon publication.
2409.08207.authors: Hao Chen, Jiafu Wu, Ying Jin, Jinlong Peng, Xiaofeng Mao, Mingmin Chi, Mufeng Yao, Bo Peng, Jian Li, Yun Cao

2408.15235.title: Learning-based Multi-View Stereo: A Survey

screening.reason: This is a survey of learning-based MVS methods that includes large feed-forward methods (the category containing DUSt3R) as one of several families, making it useful adjacent context rather than a core contribution. It is not a dataset or benchmark, so it does not qualify as a resource.
screening.evidence: large feed-forward methods
screening.task: survey of learning-based multi-view stereo methods

2408.15235.abstract: 3D reconstruction aims to recover the dense 3D structure of a scene. It plays an essential role in various applications such as Augmented/Virtual Reality (AR/VR), autonomous driving and robotics. Leveraging multiple views of a scene captured from different viewpoints, Multi-View Stereo (MVS) algorithms synthesize a comprehensive 3D representation, enabling precise reconstruction in complex environments. Due to its efficiency and effectiveness, MVS has become a pivotal method for image-based 3D reconstruction. Recently, with the success of deep learning, many learning-based MVS methods have been proposed, achieving impressive performance against traditional methods. We categorize these learning-based methods as: depth map-based, voxel-based, NeRF-based, 3D Gaussian Splatting-based, and large feed-forward methods. Among these, we focus significantly on depth map-based methods, which are the main family of MVS due to their conciseness, flexibility and scalability. In this survey, we provide a comprehensive review of the literature at the time of this writing. We investigate these learning-based methods, summarize their performances on popular benchmarks, and discuss promising future research directions in this area.
2408.15235.authors: Fangjinhua Wang, Qingtian Zhu, Di Chang, Quankai Gao, Junlin Han, Tong Zhang, Richard Hartley, Marc Pollefeys

2408.11085.title: GS-CPR: Efficient Camera Pose Refinement via 3D Gaussian Splatting

screening.reason: The paper uses MASt3R as an off-the-shelf component for 2D matching within a 3DGS-based pose refinement framework; its main contribution is camera pose refinement for localization, not a new geometry prediction model from unposed images.
screening.evidence: utilizing the 3D foundation model, MASt3R, for precise 2D matching
screening.task: camera pose refinement for visual localization

2408.11085.abstract: We leverage 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) as a scene representation and propose a novel test-time camera pose refinement (CPR) framework, GS-CPR. This framework enhances the localization accuracy of state-of-the-art absolute pose regression and scene coordinate regression methods. The 3DGS model renders high-quality synthetic images and depth maps to facilitate the establishment of 2D-3D correspondences. GS-CPR obviates the need for training feature extractors or descriptors by operating directly on RGB images, utilizing the 3D foundation model, MASt3R, for precise 2D matching. To improve the robustness of our model in challenging outdoor environments, we incorporate an exposure-adaptive module within the 3DGS framework. Consequently, GS-CPR enables efficient one-shot pose refinement given a single RGB query and a coarse initial pose estimation. Our proposed approach surpasses leading NeRF-based optimization methods in both accuracy and runtime across indoor and outdoor visual localization benchmarks, achieving new state-of-the-art accuracy on two indoor datasets. The project page is available at https://xrim-lab.github.io/GS-CPR/.
2408.11085.authors: Changkun Liu, Shuai Chen, Yash Bhalgat, Siyan Hu, Ming Cheng, Zirui Wang, Victor Adrian Prisacariu, Tristan Braud

2406.04343.title: Flash3D: Feed-Forward Generalisable 3D Scene Reconstruction from a Single Image

screening.reason: Flash3D predicts 3D Gaussians from a single unposed image, which is a reconstructable scene representation, but it is a single-image method starting from a monocular depth foundation model rather than a multi-image pointmap-based approach like DUSt3R, making it adjacent rather than core. The single-image input setting and Gaussian Splatting architecture distinguish it from DUSt3R's core task of multi-view geometry prediction.
screening.evidence: we start from a "foundation" model for monocular depth estimation and extend it to a full 3D shape and appearance reconstructor
screening.task: single-image 3D scene reconstruction and novel view synthesis

2406.04343.abstract: We propose Flash3D, a method for scene reconstruction and novel view synthesis from a single image which is both very generalisable and efficient. For generalisability, we start from a "foundation" model for monocular depth estimation and extend it to a full 3D shape and appearance reconstructor. For efficiency, we base this extension on feed-forward Gaussian Splatting. Specifically, we predict a first layer of 3D Gaussians at the predicted depth, and then add additional layers of Gaussians that are offset in space, allowing the model to complete the reconstruction behind occlusions and truncations. Flash3D is very efficient, trainable on a single GPU in a day, and thus accessible to most researchers. It achieves state-of-the-art results when trained and tested on RealEstate10k. When transferred to unseen datasets like NYU it outperforms competitors by a large margin. More impressively, when transferred to KITTI, Flash3D achieves better PSNR than methods trained specifically on that dataset. In some instances, it even outperforms recent methods that use multiple views as input. Code, models, demo, and more results are available at https://www.robots.ox.ac.uk/~vgg/research/flash3d/.
2406.04343.authors: Stanislaw Szymanowicz, Eldar Insafutdinov, Chuanxia Zheng, Dylan Campbell, João F. Henriques, Christian Rupprecht, Andrea Vedaldi

2405.14959.title: EvGGS: A Collaborative Learning Framework for Event-based Generalizable Gaussian Splatting

screening.reason: The paper proposes a feedforward 3D Gaussian reconstruction framework, but from event streams rather than unposed RGB images, making it adjacent to the DUSt3R survey's core scope of geometry prediction from unposed images. It does not extend DUSt3R or its pointmap-based geometry, nor does it operate on image inputs.
screening.evidence: reconstructs scenes as 3D Gaussians from only event input in a feedforward manner
screening.task: event-based generalizable 3D scene reconstruction

2405.14959.abstract: Event cameras offer promising advantages such as high dynamic range and low latency, making them well-suited for challenging lighting conditions and fast-moving scenarios. However, reconstructing 3D scenes from raw event streams is difficult because event data is sparse and does not carry absolute color information. To release its potential in 3D reconstruction, we propose the first event-based generalizable 3D reconstruction framework, called EvGGS, which reconstructs scenes as 3D Gaussians from only event input in a feedforward manner and can generalize to unseen cases without any retraining. This framework includes a depth estimation module, an intensity reconstruction module, and a Gaussian regression module. These submodules connect in a cascading manner, and we collaboratively train them with a designed joint loss to make them mutually promote. To facilitate related studies, we build a novel event-based 3D dataset with various material objects and calibrated labels of grayscale images, depth maps, camera poses, and silhouettes. Experiments show models that have jointly trained significantly outperform those trained individually. Our approach performs better than all baselines in reconstruction quality, and depth/intensity predictions with satisfactory rendering speed.
2405.14959.authors: Jiaxu Wang, Junhao He, Ziyi Zhang, Mingyuan Sun, Jingkai Sun, Renjing Xu

2404.07097.title: Fast Encoder-Based 3D from Casual Videos via Point Track Processing

screening.reason: TracksTo4D predicts 3D structure and camera positions from video, but its input is pre-extracted 2D point tracks rather than raw images, and it targets dynamic content specifically. This makes it adjacent to DUSt3R's core task of predicting dense geometry from unposed images rather than a direct extension of DUSt3R's model or pointmap-based geometry.
screening.evidence: we propose operating directly over 2D point tracks as input
screening.task: 3D reconstruction and camera pose estimation from dynamic casual videos

2404.07097.abstract: This paper addresses the long-standing challenge of reconstructing 3D structures from videos with dynamic content. Current approaches to this problem were not designed to operate on casual videos recorded by standard cameras or require a long optimization time. Aiming to significantly improve the efficiency of previous approaches, we present TracksTo4D, a learning-based approach that enables inferring 3D structure and camera positions from dynamic content originating from casual videos using a single efficient feed-forward pass. To achieve this, we propose operating directly over 2D point tracks as input and designing an architecture tailored for processing 2D point tracks. Our proposed architecture is designed with two key principles in mind: (1) it takes into account the inherent symmetries present in the input point tracks data, and (2) it assumes that the movement patterns can be effectively represented using a low-rank approximation. TracksTo4D is trained in an unsupervised way on a dataset of casual videos utilizing only the 2D point tracks extracted from the videos, without any 3D supervision. Our experiments show that TracksTo4D can reconstruct a temporal point cloud and camera positions of the underlying video with accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art methods, while drastically reducing runtime by up to 95\%. We further show that TracksTo4D generalizes well to unseen videos of unseen semantic categories at inference time.
2404.07097.authors: Yoni Kasten, Wuyue Lu, Haggai Maron

2611.30734.title: EgoDepth-Bench: Benchmarking Metric Depth for Egocentric Manipulation

screening.reason: The benchmark targets metric depth estimation with calibrated cameras in egocentric manipulation, which is a different task from DUSt3R's core unposed-image reconstruction; its connection to DUSt3R is only indirect through the use of MapAnything (a DUSt3R extension) as one of the evaluated models.
screening.evidence: Fine-tuning MapAnything on EgoDepth-Bench reduces metric AbsRel from 0.708 to 0.091
screening.task: benchmarking metric depth estimation for egocentric manipulation

2611.30734.abstract: We introduce EgoDepth-Bench, comprising 941,233 synchronized samples collected across 37 distinct physical environments. Each sample combines six calibrated RGB views with metric depth in the native fisheye view, reconstructed from five active-infrared stereo modules. A calibrated ball-bar confirms millimeter-level geometric accuracy, with a median error of 1.27 mm on a known sphere spacing. Environment-held-out splits enable evaluation of generalization to unseen environments. Across monocular, stereo, and multi-view models, the benchmark measures both depth accuracy and prediction coverage, including on hands and objects. Fine-tuning MapAnything on EgoDepth-Bench reduces metric AbsRel from 0.708 to 0.091 and scale-aligned AbsRel from 0.327 to 0.072 on unseen environments. These results demonstrate that EgoDepth-Bench provides effective supervision and enables rigorous evaluation of metric and relative depth estimation in egocentric manipulation. The project page provides the evaluation code and interactive RGB-depth sequences.
2611.30734.authors: Yuan Gao, Dongchen Wei, Xinyang Lin, Shuhua Cao, Xueliang Guo, Zhuohan Li, Yihao Wang

2611.28591.title: CAR3T: Generalizable Calibration-Guided Reference-View Attention Reuse for Multi-View 3D Transformers

screening.reason: CAR3T is a training-free inference acceleration technique (attention output reuse) applied to existing multi-view 3D reconstruction backbones (VGGT, DA3, π³); it does not propose a new model for predicting dense geometry from unposed images, making it tangential to the DUSt3R survey's core focus. A score of 3 would require a direct contribution to geometry prediction or a substantive extension of the DUSt3R model architecture, which is absent here.
screening.evidence: a training-free framework combining reference-view attention output reuse with offline risk calibration and online dynamic layer selection
screening.task: inference acceleration for multi-view 3D reconstruction via attention output reuse
outputs: 3D reconstruction (via accelerated forward pass of existing backbones)

2611.28591.abstract: Feed-forward multi-view 3D reconstruction relies on global attention for cross-view aggregation, but the attention cost grows quadratically with the number of views, making inference increasingly expensive for larger inputs. Existing acceleration methods compress tokens or sparsify attention, potentially losing geometric detail or restricting cross-view aggregation while leaving redundancy among attention outputs underexploited. We observe similar cross-view attention distributions in certain layers, revealing an opportunity to reduce repeated global aggregation through output reuse. However, the layers suitable for reuse vary with the input, and reusing one layer alters the features received by later layers. Similarity at individual layers therefore cannot characterize the combined effect of multiple reuse decisions on output drift. To address these challenges, we propose CAR3T, a training-free framework combining reference-view attention output reuse with offline risk calibration and online dynamic layer selection. Calibration models cumulative reuse risk, while online selection adapts reuse to each input under a calibrated budget. CAR3T retains all input tokens and attends to the keys and values of all views, reducing the core attention computation in selected layers from quadratic to linear. Experiments on VGGT, DA3, and $π^3$ show forward speedups up to $1.41\times$ with at most 100 views and $1.75\times$ on longer sequences, with accuracy trade-offs across backbones and datasets.

2611.28197.title: From Point Clouds to Engineering Models: Benchmarking Agentic 3D Reconstruction in the Built Environment

screening.reason: The paper benchmarks agentic 3D reconstruction from point clouds to BIM models in the built environment, which is a domain-specific application that does not address image-based dense geometry prediction or camera pose estimation central to DUSt3R. The inputs (existing 3D scans) and outputs (CAD/BIM models) are fundamentally different from DUSt3R's unposed-image-to-pointmap pipeline.
screening.evidence: Benchmarking Agentic 3D Reconstruction in the Built Environment
screening.task: Scan-to-BIM: converting 3D point cloud scans into engineering/BIM models using coding agents

2611.28197.abstract: Coding agents can translate 3D measurements into CAD geometry, but reconstructing engineering models for the built environment demands semantic interpretation and consistent construction constraints beyond surface fitting. We formulate scene-level Scan-to-BIM (Building Information Modeling) as an agentic 3D coding task and introduce S2Bench, comprising public and proprietary scans of 128 real-world scenes across five domains, paired with expert-curated reference models spanning diverse spatial scales. A shared framework lets agents measure scans in Python, build class-labeled components in a live CAD/BIM kernel, and iteratively refine their code. We also propose parallel asynchronous collaboration, where a lead delegates versioned tasks, continues modeling while workers execute, and integrates revision-bound proposals. Evaluating five agents and a collaborative team across 1,028 reconstructions shows that scan-to-model residuals directly guide geometric repair, whereas inferring semantic classes and construction relations requires joint geometric, visual, and engineering reasoning that agents struggle to ground and verify. Consequently, the leading agent fits scan geometry closely ($96\%$ coverage within $5\,\text{cm}$) yet reaches only $63\%$ mIoU, and no agent passes all engineering checks on more than $38\%$ of scenes. Coverage and engineering conformance drop with scene scale, whereas running a smaller model as a team improves all three axes with greater coverage gains on larger scenes. The project page is available at https://tumcms.github.io/S2Bench.github.io/

2611.28191.title: BReD: BEV Residual Diffusion for Feed-Forward Road Gaussian Reconstruction

screening.reason: BReD is a domain-specific road reconstruction method that uses calibrated (posed) camera sequences, not unposed images, and has no stated connection to DUSt3R or its pointmap-based geometry. It qualifies as a tangential 3D reconstruction method rather than a core contribution to unposed-image scene reconstruction.
screening.evidence: a feed-forward framework for reconstructing road elevation, appearance, and semantics from calibrated six-camera sequences
screening.task: feed-forward road surface reconstruction (elevation, appearance, semantics) from calibrated camera sequences

2611.28191.abstract: Accurate road surface reconstruction is essential for autonomous-driving mapping and simulation, but existing methods trade reconstruction quality for cross-scene inference. Optimization-based methods recover detailed surfaces through costly per-scene optimization, while feed-forward methods lack road-specific constraints and often produce large elevation errors. We propose \textbf{BReD}, a feed-forward framework for reconstructing road elevation, appearance, and semantics from calibrated six-camera sequences. BReD first estimates coarse elevation through LiDAR-supervised depth learning and BEV lifting, using only cameras at inference. A lightweight BEV residual diffusion model then conditions elevation refinement on a camera-derived depth--elevation discrepancy and elevation-aware image features. Diffusion-indexed perturbations expose the model to different discrepancy corruption levels during training, while inference performs one deterministic refinement from the clean discrepancy. The refined elevations are temporally aggregated to anchor road-aligned Gaussians, whose attributes are predicted by a geometry-prior-guided decoder without test-time optimization. On four held-out nuScenes scenes, BReD achieves 7.34 cm elevation RMSE and 90.92\% semantic mIoU, compared with 14.43 cm for RoGS without test-time LiDAR and 8.88 cm for its test-time-LiDAR-assisted variant; both RoGS variants require per-scene optimization.

2611.26431.title: FFGaussType: Feed-Forward Conversion of Glyph and SVG Geometry into Compact Gaussian Assets

screening.reason: The paper converts known 2D glyph and SVG geometry into 3D Gaussian assets for text/icon placement in scenes, which is a domain-specific application with no connection to reconstructing dense scene geometry from unposed images. It does not extend DUSt3R, predict pointmaps, or operate on unposed image inputs.
screening.evidence: converts extruded glyph and SVG outlines into Gaussian assets in a single forward pass
screening.task: Converting 2D glyph and SVG geometry into 3D Gaussian assets for immersive scene placement

2611.26431.abstract: Immersive 3D content allows text and graphical elements, such as subtitles, annotations, and icons, to be placed inside a scene rather than displayed as flat overlays. Placed this way, they respect occlusion and perspective and take on user-assigned materials and lighting while preserving their original shapes. In Gaussian scenes, however, each new glyph or icon requires its own iterative optimization, which limits scalable content creation. We present FFGaussType, which converts extruded glyph and SVG outlines into Gaussian assets in a single forward pass. A point encoder maps anchors sampled on the known surface to a single feature plane, from which a decoder shared by all assets predicts neural Gaussians carrying surface normals. This separates geometric conversion from material and lighting choices, and the feature plane supports image and video coding for compact delivery. We construct a paired dataset of 27,221 glyph and SVG icon assets with anchors and calibrated normal and silhouette renderings, holding out font families for evaluation. Conversion from prepared anchors takes 9.1 ms per asset, at a fraction of the compute and memory of prior baselines. On unseen font families and test icons, FFGaussType achieves $1.62^\circ$ normal error and $0.985$ silhouette IoU, the best among the compared feed-forward converters, matching the fidelity that per-asset fitting needs thousands of steps to reach. The code and dataset will be released after publication.
2611.26431.authors: Haoan Feng, Tianfu Wang, Peimeng Guan, Dae Yeol Lee, Guan-ming Su

2611.25061.title: Infer3D: Inverse Generative Modeling Enables Robust 3D Reconstruction

screening.reason: The paper proposes a test-time optimization framework for monocular 3D reconstruction, which is tangentially related to DUSt3R's multi-view unposed reconstruction task but does not directly predict dense geometry from unposed images. It is an optimization-centered method without a core DUSt3R extension or comparable feedforward geometry prediction from unposed multi-view inputs.
screening.evidence: recovers the latent variables of a generative model to best match the monocular input
screening.task: monocular 3D reconstruction via inverse generative modeling

2611.25061.abstract: Humans can understand the 3D structure of scenes even from highly unfamiliar or extreme viewpoints. Cognitive science suggests this generalization stems from a top-down generative inference strategy. In contrast, state-of-the-art 3D reconstruction neural networks typically rely on amortized, feedforward inference. While fast, this pattern-matching approach degrades when faced with out-of-distribution (OOD) scene conditions unseen during training. Inspired by the generative nature of human vision, we propose Infer3D, an inverse generative modeling framework that recovers the latent variables of a generative model to best match the monocular input. To prevent degenerate flat outputs, we couple the generative image prior with a frozen 3D lifting network that constrains the optimization space to a valid, multi-view-consistent 3D manifold. Across a variety of controlled synthetic and real-world tasks, Infer3D demonstrates superior OOD reconstruction accuracy compared to feedforward networks trained on equal or larger datasets. Furthermore, mirroring how human perception requires more time to process confusing stimuli, we introduce an adaptive inference strategy that expends more test-time compute on ambiguous OOD examples while efficiently routing in-distribution inputs. Project website: https://amanikiruga.github.io/infer3d-site/

2611.24253.title: One Shot, Any View: High-Fidelity Video Reshooting with Geometry Guidance and Visual References

screening.reason: The main contribution is a video reshooting/generation system that uses feed-forward 3D reconstruction as a geometry guidance component for a generative model, not a core geometry reconstruction contribution. The instructions explicitly list generative video as a reason for the related category.
screening.evidence: a feed-forward reconstruction of the source video
screening.task: video reshooting along a user-specified camera trajectory
inputs: optional character and scene reference images

2611.24253.abstract: Filming a scene from an additional angle after production usually requires a costly reshoot. We present One Shot Any View, a system that takes a recorded clip and generates a reshot video of the same performance along a user-specified camera trajectory. As in recent geometry-grounded methods, the system conditions generation on the source video and an explicit 3D prior, namely a point video rendered along the requested trajectory from a feed-forward reconstruction of the source video. We target human-centric cinematic videos, which are often shot with long lenses, shallow depth of field, and low-key lighting, all of which degrade feed-forward reconstruction. Existing geometry-grounded methods tend to inherit the degraded point video, and their output quality drops visibly. Two designs make such point videos usable. First, in addition to rendered videos of 3D assets, we train on real-world multi-camera videos, whose point videos are produced by the same reconstruction pipeline as at inference. This training-inference consistency enables the generator to take only the composition of people and scene elements from the point video, and their appearance from the source video. Second, a geometry-anchored RoPE offset keeps the generated video temporally synchronized with the source while largely preventing the output from copying the degraded appearance of the point video. Meanwhile, since the generator is a pretrained reference-to-video (R2V) model, the system also accepts optional character and scene reference images, which supply the appearance of regions that the source never shows. In both objective and human evaluations, One Shot Any View outperforms existing reshooting methods.

2611.24007.title: Freeforward4d: Annotation-free feed-forward 4d reconstruction of driving scenes

screening.reason: The paper is a domain-specific (driving) application that reconciles predictions from existing pretrained visual models into a consistent frame for 4D reconstruction; its main contribution is the reconciliation framework and object motion modeling rather than a general geometry prediction model from unposed images. A score of 3 is less appropriate because the geometry prediction itself relies on existing pretrained models rather than introducing a new core reconstruction method.
screening.evidence: Pretrained visual models can predict cameras, depth, and object tracks from RGB alone
screening.task: annotation-free feed-forward 4D reconstruction of driving scenes from RGB video

2611.24007.abstract: Feed-forward 4D reconstruction enables efficient creation of renderable driving scenes for autonomous driving simulation. However, most existing methods rely heavily on dataset-provided cameras, LiDAR depth, or 3D box annotations, limiting their applicability to unannotated driving videos. Pretrained visual models can predict cameras, depth, and object tracks from RGB alone, but their geometry is mutually inconsistent: multi-view predictions come in short windows with independent scales and frames, while monocular depth is metric only per image. Our key insight is that, once reconciled into a single metric frame, these priors can replace dataset annotations for feed-forward 4D reconstruction. We present \textbf{FreeForward4D}, which calibrates overlapping prediction windows against monocular metric depth and registers them into one frame across time. On this geometry, 2D tracks are associated across cameras in 3D, and objects move through hierarchical motion that combines a shared object velocity with local Gaussian corrections, so that both training and inference use only RGB videos. On Waymo, FreeForward4D achieves 27.66 dB PSNR and 0.836 SSIM while recovering metric-scale cameras and depth without scale alignment. It surpasses STORM, SLARM-F, UFO, DGGT, and StreetForward, which rely on dataset annotations, in full-image PSNR and attains the best RGB fidelity on 8-second windows. RGB-only fine-tuning further adapts the framework to nuScenes and Argoverse 2. Code will be released.
2611.24007.authors: Luosong Guo, Xiang Yang, Chaoyang Li, Ao Gao, Jiangming Shi, Yanyun Qu, Zhizhong Zhang, Jingyu Gong, Yuan Xie

2611.22207.title: ARG-Avatar: Animation-Rendering Guidance for Efficient Feedforward Avatar Reconstruction

screening.reason: This is a domain-specific application (animatable 3D human avatar reconstruction) that does not extend DUSt3R's pointmap-based geometry or directly predict comparable dense scene geometry from unposed images. It reconstructs parametric human avatars rather than general scene geometry, making it a tangential connection to the survey's core scope.
screening.evidence: Reconstructing animatable 3D human avatars from images is important for applications such as gaming and augmented reality
screening.task: feedforward 3D human avatar reconstruction from images

2611.22207.abstract: Reconstructing animatable 3D human avatars from images is important for applications such as gaming and augmented reality. Feedforward methods make avatar reconstruction accessible by reducing inference time to a few seconds, but recent approaches rely heavily on scaling model capacity, training data, and computation. We ask whether such scaling is necessary. To this end, we introduce ARG-Avatar, an efficient feedforward framework with only 68M trainable parameters that achieves SOTA reconstruction quality. Our key insight is that 3D animation and rendering already provide strong geometric correspondences that existing methods largely attempt to learn from data. In light of this, we design the Foreground Avatar Coordinate RoPE attention (FACRoPE) and Intermediate Token Rendering (ITR) pipeline to guide avatar tokens to attend to their corresponding patches. Experiments across multiple datasets show that ARG-Avatar consistently outperforms prior methods when using two or more input images. Compared with LHM++, ARG-Avatar uses approximately 9$\times$ fewer trainable parameters, 4.8$\times$ fewer training sequences, and 14$\times$ less training compute, while running 6$\times$ faster and achieving a 2.7 dB PSNR improvement on the out-of-distribution NeuMan benchmark.

2611.21126.title: IGRecon4D: Dynamic-Object-Aware Feed-Forward Reconstruction of Driving Scenes

screening.reason: This is a domain-specific (driving scenes) feed-forward reconstruction method that relies on LiDAR as a key input for Gaussian anchoring, making it a specialized application rather than a general-purpose dense geometry prediction method from unposed images comparable to DUSt3R. Score 3 is less appropriate because it does not apply or extend a core model but introduces a separate domain-specific pipeline.
screening.evidence: feed-forward dynamic scene reconstruction framework
screening.task: 4D driving-scene reconstruction with dynamic object awareness

2611.21126.abstract: Feed-forward 4D driving-scene reconstruction enables efficient modeling of dynamic autonomous-driving scenes, but current methods suffer from two complementary failure modes: semantic leakage of traffic participants into the static representation and geometric drift of Gaussian locations across viewpoints. We propose \textbf{IGRecon4D}, a feed-forward dynamic scene reconstruction framework that addresses these failures with training-time instance-prior distillation and LiDAR-anchored Gaussian positioning. Specifically, an instance-level semantic branch provides a potentially dynamic participant prior, which is distilled into dynamic-mask learning through the Instance-Dynamic Consistency Constraint to encourage high-recall localization of traffic-participant regions prone to dynamic-static leakage. In parallel, sparse LiDAR measurements guide dense depth estimation, and the resulting depths are back-projected to anchor Gaussian positions for improved multi-view geometric consistency. Experiments on the Waymo Open Dataset and zero-shot evaluation on nuScenes demonstrate improved full-image reconstruction on the main benchmark and stronger traffic-participant-region reconstruction under cross-dataset evaluation.
2611.21126.authors: Yifei Tong, Ziyang Huang, Yizhao Han, Xiaoxiao Long, Hao Zhu

2611.14218.title: ViGA-FLAME: Aligning Latent Visual and Geometric Representations for Robust 3D Head Expression Estimation

screening.reason: This is a domain-specific single-image 3D head expression estimation method using a parametric FLAME model, with no connection to DUSt3R, pointmaps, or unposed multi-view scene reconstruction. It falls under domain-specific applications without a general reconstruction contribution.

2611.14218.abstract: Estimating 3D head expression from a single image requires mapping visual appearance to underlying facial geometry. We propose ViGA-FLAME, a two-stage framework that aligns semantic visual features with a structured geometric latent space. First, a Parametric-Geometric Variational Autoencoder (PG-VAE) learns a unified representation of canonical head surfaces and FLAME parameters, supporting both detailed surface reconstruction and interpretable parameter recovery. Supervision on geometry and parameters, together with consistency between the two decoding branches, connects surface detail with parametric structure. Second, a trainable Visual-Geometric Adapter (ViGA) maps features from a pretrained semantic visual encoder into this latent space. Asymmetric attention enables ViGA to align semantic image features from the visual encoder with the structured geometric information represented in the PG-VAE latent space, without altering the original visual stream. By grounding image evidence in this latent prior, ViGA-FLAME enables robust 3D head expression estimation across severe facial deformations and large viewing angles, efficiently improving robustness over competing feed-forward methods.
2611.14218.authors: Wen Hao He, Jiacheng Wu, Jie Chen

2611.12452.title: V3DSAM: Semantic-Geometric Loop Verification and Geometry-Anchored Persistent Instance Mapping for Feed-Forward Dense SLAM

screening.reason: V3DSAM is a domain-specific SLAM application that uses VGGT-SLAM 2.0 as an off-the-shelf feed-forward geometric component and adds loop verification and instance mapping on top; it does not establish an independent core geometry contribution from unposed images.

2611.12452.abstract: To address unreliable cross-view association in long-sequence feed-forward dense SLAM, this letter presents V3DSAM, an open-vocabulary semantic dense SLAM system that establishes physical correspondences at both the scene and object levels. The system combines feed-forward geometric estimates from VGGT-SLAM 2.0 with open-vocabulary semantic observations from SAM3. We introduce semantic-geometric dual-scale loop verification, which identifies false loop closures using pixel-level bidirectional reprojection and object-level 3D spatial correspondences, without accessing backbone-internal features. We further propose geometry-anchored persistent instance mapping, which defines physical instances through class-constrained 3D connectivity in an optimized global coordinate system and assigns global IDs without inter-frame identity propagation. The proposed verifier rejects all four false loop candidates in our TUM RGB-D evaluation, while long-sequence ScanNet experiments show improved instance identity consistency. Thus, V3DSAM reduces dependence on internal backbone features and temporal ID propagation for robust long-term cross-view association.

2611.12259.title: A forensic evaluation framework for egocentric foundation models: an EFM3D case study for crime scene reconstruction

screening.reason: This is a domain-specific forensic evaluation of an existing egocentric foundation model (EFM3D) without proposing a new geometry prediction method or a general reconstruction contribution. The closest alternative score of 3 would require the paper to apply a core DUSt3R-family model to a different task, but EFM3D is not established as such a model in the supplied text.

2611.12259.abstract: Foundation models increasingly combine geometry, semantics, and spatial context for three-dimensional scene understanding, but their suitability for forensic crime scene reconstruction remains unclear. This study presents a structured forensic evaluation framework for egocentric foundation models and demonstrates it using the Egocentric Foundation Model for 3D (EFM3D). Four simulated indoor crime scenes were recorded with Meta Project Aria Gen~1 at Robert Gordon University's East Lodge House forensic training facility. The framework evaluates room-scale reconstruction, semantic scene understanding, computational performance, and forensic suitability. Across the four scenes, EFM3D generated meshes averaging $12{,}668\pm2{,}430$ vertices and $24{,}838\pm4{,}903$ faces, with 39,529 recorded semantic predictions spanning 21--24 categories at a mean confidence of 0.40. Because reference meshes and expert-labelled 3D ground truth were unavailable, these statistics are treated as descriptive outputs rather than measures of geometric or detection accuracy. Final inference runs processed $1{,}388\pm203$ snippets per scene at $0.69\pm0.01$ samples/s and required $50.77\pm6.12$ minutes per recording. A seven-criterion capability profile indicated stronger support for room geometry, furniture localisation, scene context, and spatial relationships than for fine-scale forensic evidence. The results position EFM3D as a complementary tool for contextual documentation and scene review rather than a replacement for high-fidelity forensic capture. The framework provides a reproducible basis for evaluating future egocentric foundation models in specialised forensic settings.

2611.11951.title: UltraVoxelGS: Voxel-First Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting for 3D Ultrasound Reconstruction

screening.reason: The paper is a domain-specific (ultrasound) feed-forward 3D reconstruction method that explicitly takes posed images as input, which does not meet the core requirement of unposed inputs, and it has no stated connection to DUSt3R or its pointmap-based geometry. It is tangentially related as another feed-forward 3D reconstruction approach but in a different modality and with different input assumptions.

screening.task: feed-forward 3D ultrasound reconstruction from posed images

2611.11951.abstract: We present UltraVoxelGS, a 3D ultrasound reconstruction method that achieves both fast reconstruction and physically faithful rendering for the first time, bringing live spatial feedback during 2D ultrasound scanning within reach. This is made possible by a feed-forward design that predicts a complete Gaussian scene representation from posed ultrasound images directly, entirely bypassing the per-scene optimization bottleneck that has confined prior methods to offline use. Realising such feed-forward prediction in this setting is non-trivial: unlike natural images, ultrasound slices share at most one-dimensional intersections and exhibit view-dependent appearance due to acoustic propagation and attenuation, violating the dense overlap and photometric consistency assumed by existing feed-forward Gaussian methods. Hence, to achieve fast reconstruction, we introduce a feed-forward voxel-to-Gaussian pass that decouples representation size from input count by lifting all posed slices into a fixed-size voxel support and predicting Gaussian parameters directly. For faithful rendering, we propose ultrasound-aware appearance rendering strategy factorize reflection from cumulative attenuation during training and exploit appearance continuity among spatially adjacent slices for efficient Render-time Appearance Adaptation. On both real-world and simulated datasets, UltraVoxelGS achieves best PSNR/SSIM compared with per-scene optimization baselines while reducing inference from 10-20 minutes to approximately 10 seconds (over 35 times faster) and scales to sequences exceeding 1,000 frames. Code is available at https://github.com/YuebyYue/UltraVoxelGS-camera-ready.
2611.11951.authors: Yue Wang, Haoxin Chen, Xiaoqing Guo

2611.10562.title: ZARA: Zero-shot Animatable and Relightable 3D Avatar reconstruction from a single image

screening.reason: ZARA is a domain-specific application focused on relightable human avatar reconstruction from a single image, with its main contribution being material-aware Gaussian representations rather than general dense scene geometry from unposed images. It does not establish an independent core geometry contribution aligned with DUSt3R's pointmap-based reconstruction.
screening.evidence: a zero-shot feed-forward framework that reconstructs an animatable 3D Gaussian avatar together with its intrinsic attributes from a single image
screening.task: relightable 3D human avatar reconstruction from a single image

2611.10562.abstract: Recent large human reconstruction models create remarkable animatable 3D avatars from a single image, but their appearance remains entangled with the illumination and cannot be relighted. In contrast, existing 3D relightable-avatar reconstruction methods typically require person-specific optimization. We present ZARA, a zero-shot feed-forward framework that reconstructs an animatable 3D Gaussian avatar together with its intrinsic attributes from a single image. ZARA couples a pretrained large-scale human reconstruction model with a Material Transformer to inherit geometry priors while learning material-aware Gaussian representations. To preserve localized details, we introduce Gaussian-aligned material feature fusion strategy, which injects multi-scale material features onto individual Gaussians and combines them with geometry tokens. As most human-avatar datasets lack ground-truth material maps, we use pseudo-material labels as conditioning inputs and supervision targets during training. 2611.10241.title: OfficeTwin: Realizing 3D Reconstruction of Redundant Scenes through Partial Viewpoint Perception

screening.reason: The paper is a domain-specific application (office scenes) that uses feed-forward reconstruction as a component but its main contribution is exploiting structural redundancy to produce simulation-ready assets, not a general dense geometry prediction method from unposed images.

2611.10241.abstract: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction turns an uncalibrated monocular stream into a dense point cloud in a single inference pass, orders of magnitude faster than classical structure-from-motion (e.g., COLMAP), and reliable on the weakly textured, repetitive surfaces where keypoint matching fails outright. However, raw point clouds lack the object identity, physical properties, and watertight volume required for robot learning. This gap widens under robot-native capture. A camera mounted on a robot constrained to a few degrees of freedom sees each object only partially, and the repetitive, weakly textured structure of an office makes distinct workstations nearly indistinguishable, leaving redundant and partial observations that downstream reconstruction cannot resolve. Existing image-to-3D generation methods struggle with these conditions, hallucinating geometry under incomplete views and confusing repeated instances. We present OfficeTwin, a robot-native framework that converts these incomplete observations into simulation-ready digital twins. OfficeTwin first imposes metric and structural constraints, then exploits the office's structural redundancy by registering repeated cubicles into a shared canonical frame, where complementary observations recover geometry occluded in any single view without hallucination. On a real office scan, OfficeTwin recovers every cubicle as an individually watertight, metric solid, outperforming feed-forward reconstruction and generative baselines that fail to produce simulation-ready assets.

2611.08861.title: Align3D: Image-Structure Co-Aligned 3D Scene Generation with Observability-Aware Fidelity-Preserving Guidance

2611.08861.abstract: We present Align3D, an image-conditioned diffusion model that generates 3D indoor layouts that are both faithful to a single input photograph and physically plausible beyond the observed view. From the photograph we infer a confidence-calibrated scene graph and train a set-diffusion layout denoiser with image-structure co-alignment where confidence-weighted modality fusion balances image and scene-graph alignment using predicted confidences, while observability-aware fidelity-preserving guidance projects conflicting scene-quality gradients and reweighs them with an object-level confidence mask so under-observed degrees of freedom absorb physical priors without undoing the image-graph match. On 3D-FRONT, Align3D improves image-alignment and scene-quality metrics over recent baselines; once trained, it maps previously unseen photographs to layouts in a single feed-forward pass.

2611.08330.abstract: Hand avatar reconstruction typically relies on multi-view capture or per-subject optimization, limiting its scalability. We introduce InstantHand, a feed-forward framework that constructs an animatable 3D Gaussian hand avatar from a single image using off-the-shelf MANO, camera, and mask estimates, without test-time optimization. Image-averaged losses provide insufficient supervision for alpha leakage, which thickens thin finger contours. To address this issue, we propose a Soft Alpha Band regularizer that concentrates supervision on silhouette boundaries. Furthermore, colors regressed from image features can drift toward a learned prior even in observed regions. Our Reliability-gated Appearance Transfer preserves observed appearance by transferring source colors according to each Gaussian's rendering contribution, while completing unobserved regions using the learned prior conditioned on global source identity. InstantHand constructs an avatar in 2.84 seconds and renders at 161 FPS, matching per-subject-optimized baselines on InterHand2.6M and remaining competitive in zero-shot evaluation on HanCo.

2611.07955.title: Rotation Is Token-Blind: A Structural Criterion for Post-Training Quantization of Feed-Forward Geometry Transformers

screening.reason: The paper proposes a post-training quantization framework for feed-forward geometry transformers, which is a deployment/efficiency technique applied to the class of models the survey covers, not a contribution to dense geometry prediction from unposed images itself.
screening.evidence: a structure-aware PTQ framework

2611.07955.abstract: Feed-forward 3D models use Transformers to predict camera poses, depth, and structure in one pass, avoiding iterative multi-view optimization. Long sequences and deep attention incur high compute and memory costs, motivating Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) for deployment. Existing PTQ methods mainly suppress channel-wise outliers by smoothing or orthogonal rotation. Geometry Transformers introduce a different challenge: heterogeneous token types share one activation quantization grid. A few special tokens may exert high leverage over global outputs and be updated by only a subset of blocks. Token-blind transforms, which apply the same transformation to every token, reduce overall quantization error but cannot remove differentiated degradation across token types. We propose QMapAnything, a structure-aware PTQ framework. We cast floating-point-preserving rotation and smoothing as a token-blind reparameterization group, and prove that they yield common-mode gains while leaving relative token SNR unchanged. We introduce a statistic $Γ$ that combines a special token's quantization disadvantage and output leverage to predict whether differentiated bias correction is needed beyond rotation. Experiments on geometric benchmarks show that W4A8 closely matches full-precision performance. Under W8A8, peak memory falls by $2.2$--$3.1\times$ versus FP32, with up to $3.1\times$ speedup on real hardware. These results provide a principled and efficient approach to deploying feed-forward 3D reconstruction models in resource-constrained edges.

2611.07658.abstract: Articulated 3D assets are essential for robotic simulation and training, yet their generation from casual images poses a key challenge: recovering part geometry and kinematics that remain mutually consistent. We present ArtCrafter, a novel feed-forward generative model for controllable generation of articulated 3D objects from a pair of images, one depicting the object in the rest state and the other in the open state. At the core of ArtCrafter is a DiT-based generative model that jointly produces part-level meshes for both articulation states in a single forward pass. Inspired by Slot Attention, its denoising process operates on a $1+2N$ slot layout comprising one shared base slot and $N$ paired rest/open slots, encouraging each pair to bind to the same kinematic part. To ensure geometrically consistent and disjoint part generation, we introduce Triplet Attention to enforce cross-state geometric consistency between paired rest/open slots anchored through the shared base slot, and a repulsion loss $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{rep}}$ on decoded part point clouds to prevent inter-part penetration throughout denoising. Given the resulting paired meshes, URDF joint parameters---type, axis, origin, and range---are derived analytically from the rigid transformation between each rest/open pair, providing an interpretable alternative to learned joint-parameter regression. Extensive experiments on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution datasets demonstrate that ArtCrafter outperforms existing method under the same dual-state setting in geometry quality and articulation precision, while remaining competitive with methods operating under different input settings and paradigms.

2611.06273.title: Quo Vadis, Driving Scene Reconstruction? Occlusion-Aware Gaussian Densification

screening.reason: The paper is a domain-specific driving scene reconstruction method using 3D Gaussian Splatting with a focus on occlusion-aware densification, not a general method for predicting dense geometry from unposed images. The inputs are surround-view images from a vehicle (posed cameras), and the core contribution is occlusion handling rather than the fundamental unposed geometry prediction that defines the DUSt3R core.
